audits.overall: Memory discipline is better than typical: bots are CPU-only with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' (run_pipeline.py:119) — correct for a ~1-3MB LSTM, avoiding two ~300-600MB CUDA contexts; hypersearch caches one fold at a time, caps the CUDA allocator at 40%, and halves batches on OOM; all Numba kernels use @njit(cache=True) (one-time compile, fast restarts); the GUI bounds every buffer (200 news, 5000 log blocks, 6-symbol chart cache) and never imports torch; nothing in the bot/pipeline path imports Qt, so headless operation works. Weekly retrain stops both bots first (run_pipeline.py:1121) — the "hypersearch runs while bots trade" concern does not materialize, though the backfill worker's pause flag is inverted and it runs during retrain. README's "pre-allocates full sequence tensors on GPU" (README.md:253) is stale — v2 streams batches from CPU numpy, which is better. Steady-state census: pipeline (~100-200MB) + two bots (~500-800MB each: torch+pandas+numba+sklearn per process) + backfill (~80MB) + optional GUI (~400-600MB) ≈ 1.6-2.6GB — comfortable headless. Retrain peak is the danger window. Five biggest wins: (1) stop materializing X_train in hypersearch — gather windows per batch (−~1GB peak, removes OOM-kill risk); (2) read thermal zones before tegrastats (−2-4s dead block per cycle per bot); (3) fix LLM staleness logic that collapses the 600s cadence to ~60s; (4) reuse each cycle's bar DataFrames (3-4 fetches/symbol → 1) with a persistent thread pool; (5) merge the two bots into one process (−500-800MB).

findings.title: Hypersearch materializes full fold sequence arrays (~1GB now, ~2.8GB at hard limits); unprotected by the CUDA cap
findings.evidence: SeqCache.get builds X_train = all_scaled[train_indices[:,None]+offsets] (hypersearch_v2.py:355-362). Crypto: ~285k rows (6 tickers since 2021), fold-3 train 86.6%; at seq_len=40, 22 features: 247k×40×22×4B ≈ 870MB + ~130MB val. The comment claims '~280 MB each' (319-325). adaptive_config.py:60-62 allows seq_len 64 and --max-rows defaults 500k (hypersearch_v2.py:107) → up to ~2.8GB. OOM handling catches only torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError/RuntimeError (451, 540); CPU numpy allocations bypass the 40% CUDA cap (89). PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF is setdefault AFTER set_per_process_memory_fraction lazily initializes the allocator (89-90), so expandable_segments likely never applies.
findings.impact: During Saturday retrain, CUDA context (~0.6-0.8GB) + GPU allocator (≤3GB) + fold arrays + pipeline/backfill/GUI can exceed 7.4GB; Linux overcommit means the kernel OOM-killer SIGKILLs hypersearch (uncatchable by catch=(Exception,)), pipeline retries 3x, training silently fails and bots run stale models.
findings.recommendation: Don't materialize X_train/X_val: keep only all_scaled (~25-44MB) and gather per batch in the training loop (xb = all_scaled[bi[:,None]+offsets] — same cost as today's X_train[bi] copy). Saves ~1-2.7GB peak. Also set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF before any torch.cuda call, and cap seq_len*rows product when validating adaptive expansions.

findings.title: LLM staleness check collapses 600s cadence to ~60s for the stock bot and stalls the trading loop
findings.evidence: _check_llm_staleness runs every cycle inside the LLM interval, parsing llm_analysis.json from disk (base_loop.py:461-463, 489-492) and forcing _last_llm_time=0 if the OLDEST timestamp in the section exceeds 2h (497-512). _save_analysis only updates current candidates (llm_analyst.py:124-148), and the stock bot analyzes only top_symbols (stock_loop.py:209) while GUI refresh-all writes all ~53 stock symbols into the section — so departed symbols stay stale forever. Each forced run synchronously calls call_gemini (15s timeout) + call_llm fallback + 429 sleeps (llm_client.py:453-481), plus 10 uncached Finnhub headline calls (sentiment.py:1177-1206) and fundamentals per candidate.
findings.impact: LLM batch analysis fires every ~60s instead of 600s: ~10x quota/cost burn against the $1/day cap, 5-30s+ synchronous stalls in the stock bot's money loop every other cycle, plus a 60-120KB JSON parse every 30s in both bots and the GUI.
findings.recommendation: Check staleness only for symbols in the CURRENT candidate set (or use the newest timestamp), and rate-limit forced refreshes to once per LLM_INTERVAL_SEC. Cache get_recent_headlines results (its docstring already claims it's cached). Consider moving analyze_trades to a worker thread so HTTP latency never blocks stop management.

findings.title: get_gpu_temp spawns never-exiting tegrastats with timeout=2 — guaranteed 2-4s dead block plus a killed subprocess every cycle in both bots
findings.evidence: hw_monitor.py:17-20 runs subprocess.run(['tegrastats','--interval','100'], timeout=2); tegrastats streams forever, so this ALWAYS raises TimeoutExpired after 2s and the except discards output (30-31), then falls back to thermal_zone1 (34-38). Called in base_loop._sleep every cycle (base_loop.py:907) and again on cycle%10==0 (181-184). The GUI's own _read_gpu_temp does it correctly — sysfs first, tegrastats last (gui.py:1211-1228).
findings.impact: Each bot burns 2s (4s every 10th cycle) and forks+kills a process every ~30s: ~1.6h/day of dead blocking and ~2,880 spawned processes per bot per day, for zero data. The thermal-throttle decision silently depends on thermal_zone1, which may not be the GPU zone.
findings.recommendation: Reorder: read /sys thermal zones first (match gui.py:1209-1216), drop the tegrastats path or use Popen+readline with kill. Optionally cache the temperature for 30-60s. One-line win: removes 2-4s of latency from every trading cycle on both bots.

findings.title: Same bars fetched 2-4x per symbol per cycle; correlation refresh refetches the whole universe — REST budget pressure where failed predictions force-sell crypto
findings.evidence: Per stock cycle: ~47 prediction bar fetches + SPY (base_loop.py:432-455; predict_now.py:140) ≈ 116 req/min. Buy path refetches the same symbol's bars in _compute_position_size (base_loop.py:626-635), again in _place_and_track_buy (871-880), plus get_live_atr's 60 bars (859; stock_loop.py:396). Every 10th cycle, _update_correlations serially refetches all ~47 symbols (portfolio.py:73-88; base_loop.py:175-178) then runs 1,081 LedoitWolf fits (portfolio.py:34-58); declared _corr_cache is never used (portfolio.py:14-15). ThreadPoolExecutor is recreated every cycle (432). Alpaca limit is ~200 req/min; bursts exceed it.
findings.impact: Periodic 429s degrade prediction coverage; in the crypto loop a None prediction is treated as a sell signal (base_loop.py:534-541), so rate-limit bursts can liquidate positions. Also adds seconds of serial latency per buy and per 5-minute refresh.
findings.recommendation: Cache bars per symbol per cycle: predictions already fetch them — pass the DataFrame (or a cycle-scoped dict) into sizing/ATR/GARCH instead of refetching. Reuse one persistent ThreadPoolExecutor. Reuse prediction-fetch returns for the correlation matrix instead of a second universe sweep, and honor the declared 3600s corr cache.

findings.title: Two bot processes each carry the full torch+pandas+numba+sklearn stack — merging saves ~500-800MB
findings.evidence: Census: run_pipeline + crypto_loop + stock_loop + sentiment_history --backfill (run_pipeline.py:846-887), plus optional GUI. Both bots import torch via base_loop→predict_now (predict_now.py:14) and hw_monitor (hw_monitor.py:9), plus pandas/numba (indicators.py), sklearn, arch, hmmlearn. run_pipeline's own comments estimate 300-500MB per bot (316-318); on the CUDA-build torch wheel 500-800MB RSS each is realistic. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' (119) correctly avoids 2 CUDA contexts — choose_inference_device() is hardwired to CPU (trading_utils.py:56-64), appropriate for a ~1-3MB LSTM with ms-level CPU inference.
findings.impact: ~1.0-1.6GB of the 7.4GB budget is duplicated interpreter+library+model state. That headroom is exactly what the retrain window and GUI need; it also doubles Numba cache loads and JIT warmup at startup.
findings.recommendation: Run both loops in one process (two threads or a single scheduler alternating crypto 24/7 and stock market-hours), or extract a single inference daemon both loops query. Keep CPU inference — GPU is not justified for these model sizes and would add a ~300-600MB context per process.

findings.title: Stock harvest peak holds ~3x the dataset in RAM; hypersearch loads all ~50 columns to use 22
findings.evidence: Incremental harvest keeps `existing` (full prior dataset, ~44 tickers x ~10y x ~16 bars/day x ~50 float64 cols, est. 0.5-1GB), builds all_data feature frames, then pd.concat copies again (harvest_stock_data.py:129-165). validate_training_data adds a select_dtypes copy + np.isinf mask (data_utils.py:216-219), and save writes BOTH parquet and a full CSV (data_utils.py:93-99). yfinance refetches 730d per ticker every run regardless of incremental start (data_sources.py:152-156). hypersearch then loads the full parquet with no column pushdown despite load_training_data supporting columns= (hypersearch_v2.py:121-130; data_utils.py:35-51), before capping to 200k rows.
findings.impact: Harvest peak plausibly 2-3GB — tight with GUI/backfill resident, risking swap/OOM-kill during retrain windows; ~90% of harvested rows are dead weight for training (200k cap) yet cost full feature recompute, RAM, and duplicate CSV disk every run.
findings.recommendation: Process per-ticker: append each ticker's frame to parquet incrementally instead of holding existing+all_data+concat. Drop the CSV duplicate (parquet is canonical). Pass columns=[preset features + targets + Ticker] in hypersearch's load (cuts load peak ~40-60%). Bound yfinance fetch to the incremental start date.

findings.title: fetch_crypto_volume: 6 serial uncached HTTP calls every 30s feeding a value nothing reads
findings.evidence: Every crypto cycle calls fetch_crypto_volume over the universe (crypto_loop.py:142-148): one urllib request per symbol, timeout=5, no cache (market_data.py:35-67). Grep shows the injected snapshots['Volume_Ratio'] has no consumer — buy gates read only SMA_20/ATR/Hurst (base_loop.py:762-784); predict_now's snapshot Volume_Ratio comes from its own bars, and the model never sees the injected value since prediction already completed.
findings.impact: ~17,000 wasted CryptoCompare requests/day and up to 30s of serial stall per cycle when the endpoint is slow, inside the 24/7 money loop, for a feature with zero effect on decisions.
findings.recommendation: Delete the per-cycle call, or if Volume_Ratio is meant to gate buys, actually consume it and cache results for >=5 minutes (volume ratios change slowly on hourly bars). If retained, fetch concurrently with the existing prediction ThreadPoolExecutor rather than serially after it.

findings.title: Unbounded bot stdout logs (~25-40MB/day) plus multi-process RotatingFileHandler on one trader.log
findings.evidence: Bot stdout appends to crypto/stock_bot_output.log with no rotation (run_pipeline.py:305-310). predict_now prints 4-6 lines per symbol per cycle ('--- ANALYZING ---', price, prediction, recommendation; predict_now.py:135, 232-240) — the stock bot emits ~190-280 lines/30s ≈ 25-40MB/day. Separately, every process (pipeline, both bots, backfill, GUI) attaches a DEBUG-level RotatingFileHandler to the same logs/trader.log (log_config.py:36-45); concurrent rotation across processes races and truncates/loses records.
findings.impact: Gigabytes of log growth over weeks fills the Jetson's SD/NVMe and adds constant small-write wear; cross-process rotation races corrupt the shared log right when post-incident forensics need it.
findings.recommendation: Silence per-symbol prints behind a verbosity flag (or log at DEBUG to the rotating logger only). Rotate bot stdout logs (e.g., pipe through logging or restart-truncate at 50MB). Give each process its own log file, or use a socket/queue handler — RotatingFileHandler is not multi-process safe.

findings.title: GUI LLM-refresh subprocesses: undrained stdout PIPE can deadlock a ~300-400MB child forever
findings.evidence: Both refresh paths spawn a fresh interpreter with stdout=subprocess.PIPE that is never read (gui.py:2595-2600 single-symbol; 2658-2668 refresh-all; the 'count symbols done from output' comment at 2685 is unimplemented). refresh_all imports yfinance/pandas (llm_analyst.py:151-167) and prints per-batch/per-symbol plus llm_client lines across ~20 batches (llm_analyst.py:573-640) — easily exceeding the ~64KB pipe buffer on a verbose run.
findings.impact: When the pipe fills, the child blocks forever: a transient ~300-400MB interpreter becomes permanently resident on the 8GB box, the poll timer spins indefinitely, and the button stays disabled. Refresh-one and refresh-all can also run concurrently (no mutual exclusion), doubling the transient.
findings.recommendation: Use stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL (or a log file), or read the pipe from the poll timer. Add a watchdog timeout that kills the child after N minutes, and a mutex so only one refresh subprocess exists at a time.

findings.title: GUI main-thread stalls: optuna.load_study x2 every 60s, blocking Fear&Greed fetch, perpetual article re-scoring
findings.evidence: _refresh_models_tab runs on a 60s main-thread timer (gui.py:1615-1617) and calls _get_best_score per model — each call optuna.load_study against the study SQLite (83-95), importing optuna+sqlalchemy (~80-150MB resident) and querying all trials, potentially lock-contending while hypersearch writes. on_account (10s tick) calls get_fear_greed() on the main thread (3625-3627) — a blocking requests.get(timeout=5) every ~5min when the 300s cache expires. fetch_news's upgrade filter compares _scored_by_model to 'gemini-3.1-pro-preview' (961-963), a name never assigned (sentiment.py assigns 2.5-family), so already-scored articles perpetually re-enter the 10-slot upgrade window.
findings.impact: Periodic UI freezes up to several seconds; ~100MB+ avoidable GUI residency; one gemini-2.5-pro call per 5-minute news tick (~288/day) burning the shared $1/day cap on cosmetic display scores that compete with trade-time analysis.
findings.recommendation: Move study reads to the fetcher thread and cache best_value for >=5 min (or parse it from pipeline_status.json, which already carries best_score). Move FnG into the fetcher. Fix the upgrade filter to the actually-assigned model names and skip articles already pro-scored.

findings.title: Per-cycle executor recreation forces fresh SQLite connections + schema scripts in prediction threads; article cache unbounded
findings.evidence: ThreadPoolExecutor is rebuilt every cycle (base_loop.py:432), so worker threads are new each cycle. Stock predictions call get_live_daily_sentiment per symbol (predict_now.py:169-188) → _get_db() opens a NEW thread-local sqlite3 connection and runs executescript(_SCHEMA) with up to 3 retries sleeping 2s on lock contention (sentiment_history.py:75-94) — ~5 connections+schema runs per cycle, ~14k/day, against a WAL DB shared with the backfill writer. Separately, sentiment._article_cache is a never-evicted dict of URL→2KB bodies (sentiment.py:276-277, 369-371), growing indefinitely in the 24/7 crypto bot and backfill worker; KW-fallback fetches up to 30 bodies serially at timeout=5 inside the buy-path sentiment_gate (sentiment.py:864-883).
findings.impact: Constant connection/schema churn and possible 2-6s stalls inside prediction workers when the DB is locked; tens of MB of slow per-process cache growth over weeks; a worst-case ~150s buy-path stall when the LLM is down and articles are uncached.
findings.recommendation: Create one persistent ThreadPoolExecutor in __init__; run schema creation once per process, not per connection. Bound _article_cache (e.g., 500-entry LRU). Parallelize or cap the keyword-fallback body fetches (reuse _fetch_full_texts's 10-thread pool) so sentiment_gate can never block a cycle for minutes.

audits.overall: This is an impressively engineered hobby system with real strengths: (1) genuine microstructure awareness — spread-aware limit pricing, a should_trade spread gate, winner's-curse and Hurst filters (order_utils.py:60-83,261-269; base_loop.py:757-784); (2) unusually broad risk plumbing — VIX/drawdown/correlation/leveraged-ETF scaling, stablecoin depeg checks, hard-stop lockouts, circuit breaker; (3) the training objective is directionally right — a cost-adjusted Sharpe with a fold-variance penalty and train-only scaler fitting, far better than the F1 objective the stale README describes; (4) full decision journaling (JSONL + trade_memory) that could power proper analysis. But the strategy core is unvalidated and economically incoherent. There is no backtest of the actual trading policy anywhere in the repo; models are selected by a simulator whose mechanics (overlapping 12-48-bar returns counted as independent trades, 5bps costs, ticker-blocked 'walk-forward' folds that leak across correlated symbols) inflate Sharpe and bear no resemblance to live execution. Crypto faces a ~55-80bps round-trip cost hurdle (Alpaca Tier 1: 15bps maker/25bps taker per side, docs.alpaca.markets/us/docs/crypto-fees) that neither training nor the live gate prices. The model predicts multi-day returns while stocks are force-flattened intraday — forfeiting the overnight premium where high-beta returns concentrate. Position size is never defined as risk-relative-to-equity; a miscalibrated GARCH target (2% per hourly bar) silently doubles nearly every position, and the multiplier stack can reach ~32x base with per-symbol caps unenforced for new positions. Priority one: build an event-driven backtest of the real policy with real fees before any further model tuning.

findings.title: No strategy-level backtest; model selection uses an unrealizable trade simulator
findings.evidence: Repo-wide grep for 'backtest' returns nothing outside tests/. Selection score = compute_sharpe (hypersearch_v2.py:258-280): every bar with |pred|>threshold earns the FULL 12-48-bar forward return as an independent trade — overlapping, serially-correlated returns annualized via sqrt(trade_freq*1638) as if i.i.d., inflating Sharpe by roughly sqrt(forward_bars). 1638 bars/year is the stock count, applied to 24/7 crypto (8760). The simulated policy (flip long/short every bar, no stops, no cooldown, no flatten) shares nothing with the live loop.
findings.impact: Deployed models have never been evaluated on simulated P&L of the actual policy with actual costs. 'Sharpe 2-3' trial scores are statistical artifacts; the system trades real (paper) money on an unvalidated edge.
findings.recommendation: Build an event-driven backtest replaying the live loop (entry gates, multiplier stack, cooldowns, ATR stops, 15:50 flatten, fees 25bps/side crypto + spread) over held-out months. Use non-overlapping or position-aware returns in compute_sharpe (hold fb bars, one position per symbol), and annualize crypto with 8760. Gate weekly model promotion on backtest P&L, not trial score.

findings.title: Walk-forward folds split across tickers, not time — cross-asset leakage; deployed artifact is one fold
findings.evidence: get_walk_forward_folds builds all_valid by concatenating per-ticker index ranges in ticker order (hypersearch_v2.py:224-227), then slices positionally at 60/73/86% (233-246). With ~6 tickers, 'train' = first ~3.6 tickers' full 2021-2026 history and 'val' = the next ticker's history over the SAME calendar period. The seq_len embargo is meaningless across a ticker boundary. The saved model is the single best fold's weights+scaler (654-658, 702-708), never retrained on all data.
findings.impact: Highly correlated crypto/stock series make validation contemporaneous with training — inflated scores and hyperparameters tuned to leakage. A best-fold-0 model may never have trained on tickers it trades live.
findings.recommendation: Sort indices chronologically across tickers (global timestamp order) before slicing folds, keeping per-ticker seq_len warmup exclusions; embargo in time units. After selection, retrain the chosen config on all data up to a final holdout. Report holdout-only metrics.

findings.title: Crypto edge cannot plausibly clear the real fee hurdle; cost model off ~10x and live gate is fee-blind
findings.evidence: Alpaca Tier 1 crypto fees: 15bps maker / 25bps taker per side (docs.alpaca.markets/us/docs/crypto-fees). Entries are mid+5bps limits with 30s timeout then MARKET fallback (order_utils.py:88-115,199-220); stop/breaker exits are market (base_loop.py:386-389) — mostly taker. Round trip ≈ 50bps fees + 5-30bps spread (wider on weekends). Training charges 5bps (hypersearch_v2.py:255); the live gate should_trade requires only |pred| > 2*spread_pct with NO fee term (order_utils.py:261-269); trade_threshold is tuned in [0.05,1.0]% (hypersearch_v2.py:426-427).
findings.impact: A perfectly calibrated +0.15% (live default threshold) forecast nets ≈ -0.45% per round trip at Tier 1 fees. Crypto loop is negative-expectancy by construction; if Alpaca paper fills omit fees, paper P&L silently overstates live results.
findings.recommendation: Set TRANSACTION_COST_BPS ≈ 55-80 (crypto) in compute_sharpe, and add a fee term to should_trade: required_edge = 2*(taker_fee_bps*2 + spread_bps)/100. Floor trade_threshold near 0.6-0.8% for crypto or switch to maker-only resting orders with no market fallback. Re-tune; expect far fewer, larger-edge trades.

findings.title: None-prediction path: forced sells plus ungated buys; crypto bar fetch can silently zero all predictions
findings.evidence: _execute_sells treats a missing prediction as a sell signal ('no prediction', base_loop.py:533-541). In _execute_buys, the should_trade and threshold gates sit inside 'if pred_return is not None and quote is not None' (766-770), so pred=None proceeds to sizing and buys with confidence=1.0 (618-621); model-missing mode even logs 'Running without prediction gating' (221-222). Crypto inference fetches only 120 bars (market_data.py:72-75) while SMA_100/Hurst/ATR_Percentile need 100-bar warmup (indicators.py:536-555) and df.dropna() (predict_now.py:162) leaves ~20 rows — any seq_len > ~20 (search range 8-40) returns None for every symbol.
findings.impact: A retrain landing seq_len>20, or transient data failures, turns the crypto bot into an ungated churner: buy all symbols, sell them after the 60-min cooldown for 'no prediction', repeat — paying ~55-80bps per round trip, indefinitely and silently.
findings.recommendation: Make None predictions a hard no-trade in both directions: skip buys unless pred >= threshold; skip 'no prediction' sells (keep stops active). Fetch limit = 100 + max seq_len + buffer (~250 bars) in fetch_bars_alpaca, and dropna only on model feature_cols. Alert when >50% of universe predictions are None.

findings.title: Horizon mismatch: model predicts 12-48-bar returns but positions are forced out intraday / on 60-min flips
findings.evidence: Targets are Target_Return_{fb} for fb in [12,18,24,32,48] hourly bars (harvest_stock_data.py:111-116; hypersearch_v2.py:78) — roughly 2-7 trading days for stocks. Yet flatten_before_close exits every stock position at 15:50 ET daily (stock_loop.py:141-181), capping holds at ~6 hours, and crypto exits whenever pred < -threshold after a 60-min cooldown (base_loop.py:533-541, crypto_loop.py:39). Nothing aligns holding period with forward_bars.
findings.impact: The strategy pays full round-trip costs to capture a small, early fraction of the move the model was optimized to predict; the selected horizon's edge (if any) is structurally unharvestable, and the per-trade signal-to-noise at the realized ~hours horizon is far worse than the trained horizon.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) constrain forward_bars to the realizable hold (≤6 RTH bars for stocks; ≈ cooldown-to-cooldown for crypto) and re-tune, or (b) let winners run to the horizon: hold overnight via server-side stops instead of flattening. Make the backtest (finding 1) measure realized capture ratio per horizon.

findings.title: Daily 15:50 flatten forfeits the overnight premium on a high-beta book — and still leaks overnight exposure on half-days
findings.evidence: All stock positions are sold 15:50-16:00 daily (stock_loop.py:41-42,141-181), guaranteeing 2 spread crossings/day/position (sell at mid-10bps limit, then market fallback). The literature (Lou, Polk & Skouras 2019 JFE) shows US equity returns — especially high-beta/momentum names like this universe (IONQ, QBTS, MSTR, MARA, SOXL, TQQQ; stock_universe.json) — accrue almost entirely overnight, with intraday ≈ flat. Meanwhile check_market_hours hardcodes a 16:00 close with no holiday/half-day calendar (stock_loop.py:80-91; repo-wide grep finds no get_clock/get_calendar): on 13:00 early closes the flatten never runs and day-TIF bracket legs expire, leaving unprotected overnight positions.
findings.impact: Long-only intraday exposure on high-beta names holds the part of the day with ~zero expected drift while paying ~10-30bps/day/position in crossings (~1.5-3.5%/yr on a $50k book) — and the gap-risk rationale is undermined on exactly the holiday-adjacent days when gaps are likeliest.
findings.recommendation: Use api.get_clock()/get_calendar() to drive the flatten time. Then quantify in the backtest whether flattening beats holding with server-side GTC stops; if intraday-only is retained, the model must be trained on intraday (open-to-3:50pm) targets, not multi-day returns.

findings.title: No equity/ATR-relative risk per trade; GARCH 'vol target' of 2% per hourly bar doubles nearly every position; stack reaches ~32x base with caps unenforced
findings.evidence: Size = Kelly base (up to 3x notional) x VIX x drawdown x confidence(0.5-2) x GARCH(0.5-2) x macro x corr x HMM(0.3-1.2) x sentiment(0.15-1.5) x LLM(0.65-1.5) (base_loop.py:583-691,816-828). compute_vol_adjusted_size targets 2% PER-BAR vol on hourly sigma (volatility.py:130-149, called base_loop.py:640-642): BTC/most stocks run 0.3-1%/hour, so ratio clamps at 2.0x almost always — a constant size doubler, not vol targeting. MAX_NOTIONAL_PER_SYMBOL is checked only when symbol already held (748-752); stock MAX_EXPOSURE is checked before, not net of, each order (stock_loop.py:312); crypto has no portfolio cap. Stop distance never feeds sizing.
findings.impact: Worst-case single new order ≈ 32x base ($32k crypto / $162k stock); routine orders run 2-4x intent. Dollar risk per trade (notional x 5-15% stop) floats freely between ~$100 and ~$5k+ with no relation to equity — the opposite of fixed-fractional risk budgeting.
findings.recommendation: Define risk first: notional = (equity x risk_pct, e.g. 0.5%) / stop_dist, then apply multipliers as a final factor clamped to [0.25, 1.5]. Enforce MAX_NOTIONAL_PER_SYMBOL on every order (new and add) and a crypto exposure cap. Fix target_vol to a per-hour figure (~0.3-0.5%) or convert sigma to daily before targeting.

findings.title: Kelly fraction computed from a censored trade sample: only stop/veto exits are recorded
findings.evidence: record_trade is called only in _manage_stops (base_loop.py:392,414) and _execute_llm_veto_sells (574). Signal-driven sells (_execute_sells, base_loop.py:531-552; stock_loop.py:247-290), the 15:50 flatten (stock_loop.py:141-181), server-side bracket/trailing stop fills (stock_loop.py:471-477), and emergency flattens never record. compute_kelly_fraction builds win-rate/win-loss from this trade_memory.json sample and activates at 50 trades, scaling notional up to 3x (trading_utils.py:117-187).
findings.impact: For stocks the dominant exits (flatten, bracket fills) are invisible, so Kelly's win-rate is estimated from a biased subsample (guaranteed -5% hard stops vs +15% TPs). Once 50 such trades accumulate, the whole book is sized off statistics unrelated to realized P&L — typically over-sizing.
findings.recommendation: Record every exit path (flatten, signal sell, bracket fill, emergency) into trade_memory, or better, derive Kelly inputs from the broker's fill history / daily JSONL journal which already captures all decisions. Until coverage is complete, disable the Kelly multiplier.

findings.title: Stops and take-profits are decorative in practice: floors swallow the ATR logic, TP is unreachable, trailing is inert
findings.evidence: stop_dist = clamp(2-2.5 x hourly_ATR / price, floor, ceil) with floors 5% (stock) / 6% (crypto) (stock_loop.py:61-65; crypto_loop.py:45-49; base_loop.py:355-364). Hourly ATR on majors is ~0.3-1% of price, so raw 2xATR ≈ 0.6-2.5% and the floor binds — effectively a fixed stop ~5-15x hourly ATR. TP = 3x stop = 15-30% above entry (TAKE_PROFIT_RR=3.0), unreachable within a same-day stock hold or a cooldown-driven crypto hold. Trailing activates at +1% but trails 5-10%, so it can give back to below entry; the hard stop fires first. README claims 2x stop/1.5x trail/2:1 TP — code says 2.5x/2.0x/3:1.
findings.impact: Realized exits are dominated by the EOD flatten (stocks) and prediction flips (crypto); the advertised 3:1 reward:risk geometry never materializes. Risk per trade is a fixed ~5-6% of notional regardless of asset vol, and intraday stops almost never protect anything.
findings.recommendation: Size stops off the realized holding horizon: for intraday stocks, ~2-3x hourly ATR uncapped by a 5% floor (floor ~1%); cap TP at what the horizon can deliver (~1-3%) or drop the TP leg and let the flatten/trail exit. Reconcile README with code so risk numbers are reviewable.

findings.title: Circuit breaker flattens the shared account from either bot, re-trips hourly, and fails open
findings.evidence: Drawdown = (last_equity - equity)/last_equity vs Alpaca's previous-close equity (order_utils.py:321-335); on trip, emergency_flatten cancels ALL account orders and market-sells ALL positions — both bots share one account (340-367) — then the tripped bot sleeps 3600s (base_loop.py:285). Since last_equity only resets at the next daily close, the realized -5% re-trips every hour, re-cancelling the other bot's bracket legs each time and desyncing its positions dict. API errors return (False, 0.0) — fail-open (333-335). Over weekends last_equity is Friday's close, so the crypto 'daily' breaker measures multi-day drawdown.
findings.impact: One bad crypto hour liquidates the stock book at market (and vice versa), locks the loss, then strips protective orders hourly for the rest of the day. The stop-leg cancellation leaves any restored positions unprotected.
findings.recommendation: Persist a tripped_until timestamp (end of trading day) instead of sleep(3600); scope flattening to the bot's own asset class; on API error fail closed (skip new buys). Consider a halt-new-entries breaker at 3-4% before the flatten-everything level at 5-6%.

findings.title: Top-10 by raw predicted return concentrates the book in the highest-volatility correlated names; no portfolio vol target
findings.evidence: ranked = sorted(preds.items(), key=value) takes top 10 by raw predicted return (stock_loop.py:228-229). Predicted-return magnitude scales with asset vol, so a return-regression systematically ranks IONQ/QBTS/MARA/MSTR/SOXL/TQQQ-type names (46-stock universe, stock_universe.json) above quality names. The only diversification controls: reject if avg pairwise |corr| > 0.7 and a 0.5-floor sizing factor, both estimated from 30 hourly bars via LedoitWolf (portfolio.py:17-58,127-147) — standard error ~±0.18 per pair. No portfolio-level vol or beta budget exists; the $50k cap is notional.
findings.impact: The 'diversified top-10' is effectively one leveraged high-beta/crypto-beta bet; on risk-off days all 10 positions draw down together, which is what feeds the 5% circuit breaker. Portfolio vol is unmanaged and regime-dependent.
findings.recommendation: Rank by vol-adjusted prediction (pred / GARCH or ATR sigma) instead of raw pred; estimate correlations on >=120 bars or daily returns; add a simple portfolio vol target (scale gross exposure so Σ w_i*sigma_i hits e.g. 1%/day). Cap combined crypto-proxy exposure (MARA+MSTR+COIN+HOOD+crypto).

findings.title: Sentiment gate never blocks trades despite documented hard block; half the regime/vol machinery is dead code
findings.evidence: sentiment_gate clamps to [0.15, 1.5] (sentiment.py:1172) so the documented 'news <= -0.3 blocks trades' cannot happen; the gate<=0 skip branches are unreachable (base_loop.py:811, stock_loop.py:368). Direction is defensible: greed-only FnG reduction (0.7x at >=90, no fear-side cut to avoid double-counting the model's Daily_Sentiment feature, sentiment.py:1118-1133) and news-momentum scaling consistent with short-horizon drift evidence. Meanwhile HMM threshold_mult/stop_mult are computed but never consumed (only sizing_mult, base_loop.py:660-662), get_garch_stop is imported but never called (base_loop.py:40), and _smooth_regime is inverted — it returns the neutral default instead of the previous regime and allows instant switches (regime_detector.py:177-195).
findings.impact: Catastrophic news (hack/fraud, score <=-0.5) still buys at 0.15x rather than blocking — contrary to spec and operator expectation. The regime detector's risk outputs and GARCH stops add compute and complexity with no effect, and the broken smoother randomly neutralizes the one wired output.
findings.recommendation: Decide and align: either implement a true block (return 0.0 below -0.5 and honor it) or fix the docs. Delete or wire threshold_mult/stop_mult and get_garch_stop. Fix _smooth_regime to require N consecutive observations of the NEW label, falling back to the PREVIOUS regime meanwhile.

findings.title: Crypto 24/7 execution ignores weekend liquidity decay with fixed clips and market fallbacks
findings.evidence: The crypto loop runs identically 24/7 (check_market_hours always True, crypto_loop.py:58-59) with fixed $1000 clips (line 35). Weekend/overnight Alpaca crypto spreads widen materially; the only defense is should_trade's 2x-spread gate (order_utils.py:261-269) and the wide-spread limit offset (order_utils.py:74-78) — but unfilled limits market-fallback after 30s (manage_order_lifecycle, order_utils.py:199-220), crossing the full widened spread plus 25bps taker. Stops also exit at market regardless of session (base_loop.py:386-389). Day-of-week features exist in training but no execution-level weekend policy exists.
findings.impact: Fills cluster at the worst-liquidity hours at fixed size, adding maybe 10-30bps of extra cost per weekend round trip on top of the already-unpriced fee hurdle; stop exits in thin books realize extra slippage.
findings.recommendation: Add a session-aware policy: skip market fallback (let unfilled limits cancel) when spread_pct exceeds a per-symbol cap (e.g., 2x its 30-day median), and scale clip size by inverse spread. Cheap to implement with data already in get_quote.

findings.title: Walk-forward folds split across symbols, not time — train and val cover the same calendar period
findings.evidence: load_data builds per-ticker contiguous blocks (hypersearch_v2.py:177-199); get_walk_forward_folds slices positional 60/73/86% of that ticker-blocked index list (213-246). Fold-0 train = first tickers' full 2021-2026 history; val = later tickers' history over the SAME dates. Embargo = seq_len positions only (78, 219) and is smaller than the label horizon forward_bars up to 48 (404), so train labels also overlap val features at the cut ticker.
findings.impact: Validation Sharpe measures cross-sectional memorization of one shared market period across highly correlated assets, not forward generalization. Every hyperparameter, threshold, and deployed model is selected on leaked signal; live results are disconnected from search scores.
findings.recommendation: Split by time globally: pick calendar cutoff timestamps, assign every ticker's bars to train/val by timestamp so all symbols appear on both sides, and purge train labels within forward_bars + seq_len bars of each boundary.

findings.title: Crypto live inference fetches too few bars — predictions ~24h stale or None for seq_len > ~20, then ungated trading
findings.evidence: fetch_bars_alpaca: start=now-6d, limit=120 (market_data.py:85-86). 24/7 crypto has ~144 hourly bars in 6 days and Alpaca returns ascending, so the fetched window ends ~24h before now. Features need ~100-bar warmup (SMA_100, Hurst window=100; indicators.py:536,555) and predict_now.py:162 dropna()s ALL columns, leaving ~20 rows vs tuned seq_len 8-40 (expandable to 64, adaptive_config.py:21,60). On None, base_loop sells positions as 'no prediction' (base_loop.py:533-541) while buys bypass the threshold gate (766-770).
findings.impact: Crypto bot trades day-old signals at best; with seq_len >= 22 every prediction is None — positions are churned hourly with zero model gating, paying spread continuously.
findings.recommendation: Fetch >= warmup + seq_len + buffer (e.g., 250 bars over 12 days) and keep the most recent bars (slice tail / request descending). Assert df.index.max() is within ~2h of now and return None (and never buy) when stale.

findings.title: Multi-source merge corrupts the stock bar grid (adjusted :30 yfinance interleaved with unadjusted :00 Alpaca) and inverts source priority
findings.evidence: fetch_with_fallback always concatenates Alpaca + yfinance (+CryptoCompare) and dedups keep='last' (data_sources.py:185-187) — last-listed lowest-quality source wins, opposite the docstring (112). yf.download has auto_adjust unpinned (defaults True on yfinance>=1.0) with prepost=True for stocks (148-152). Stock yf 1h bars are :30-aligned vs Alpaca :00-aligned, so timestamps never collide and both grids interleave for the ~730-day yf window. Crypto :00 bars do collide, so CryptoCompare overrides Alpaca — while inference serves Alpaca bars (predict_now.py:144-146).
findings.impact: Most recent ~2 years of stock training data has ~30-min effective bar spacing plus adjusted/unadjusted zigzags: indicator windows and Target_Return_fb mean different wall-clock spans across the dataset. Crypto trains on CryptoCompare prices but predicts on Alpaca bars.
findings.recommendation: Use yfinance only to fill timestamps Alpaca lacks; pin auto_adjust=False and drop prepost; resample everything onto one hourly grid per asset class; honor priority via dedup keep='first' or reversed concat order.

findings.title: Label horizon (12-48 bars) is unrealizable by the bots; inference window also one bar out of phase with training
findings.evidence: Targets are fb-bar forward returns with fb searched in 12-48 (harvest_stock_data.py:111-113; hypersearch_v2.py:404). The stock bot flattens everything at 15:50 ET (stock_loop.py:41-42,141-147) — max hold one session (~6.5 bars); crypto exits via ATR stops/60-min cooldowns. Training windows end at bar idx-1 with the label measured from Close[idx] (hypersearch_v2.py:358-362), but inference feeds the last seq_len rows including the current in-progress bar and treats output as return from the current price (predict_now.py:198,231-233).
findings.impact: trade_threshold and search Sharpe were optimized for 12-48 hour holds the bots never realize — stock signals predict returns extending days past the forced same-day exit; partial-bar features add systematic noise.
findings.recommendation: Restrict forward_bars to realizable horizons (stocks <= 6 RTH bars; crypto near median stop/TP exit time) or simulate the actual exit policy inside compute_sharpe. At inference, drop the in-progress bar and use completed bars only, matching training alignment.

findings.title: Deployed model is a single fold's weights, selected, early-stopped, and gated on the same validation data; no test set
findings.evidence: Best epoch per fold chosen by val loss (hypersearch_v2.py:627-634); fold Sharpe computed on the same val set (648); the single best fold's weights + that fold's scaler are cached (654-658,702-708) and shipped as production (899-929) without refit on full data. Optuna maximizes the same val Sharpes over hundreds of trials, and the save gate compares against adaptive best_score (896-899). Early-stop metric is unweighted huber delta=1.0 while training uses weighted trial-delta Huber (509,532,602).
findings.impact: Triple use of the validation set across ~200+ trials guarantees optimistic selection; a fold-0 winner trained on the first ~60% of ticker blocks may never have seen several symbols it then trades.
findings.recommendation: Reserve a final untouched time slice (e.g., most recent 2 months) scored once, only for the winning config; then retrain that config on train+val with a refit scaler and gate deployment on holdout performance.

findings.title: Sharpe objective: overlapping fb-bar trades counted independently, sqrt(fb) scale bias, stock annualization applied to crypto, broken regime penalty
findings.evidence: compute_sharpe treats every bar with |pred|>threshold as an independent trade earning the full fb-bar forward return, annualized by trade_freq*1638 (stock RTH bars/year) even for 24/7 crypto (hypersearch_v2.py:266-280). fb-bar returns scale mean~fb, std~sqrt(fb), so scores grow ~sqrt(fb), mechanically favoring fb=48. Regime labels cumsum overlapping fb-bar returns as 1-bar returns against ±2% thresholds (294-302), and the penalty evaluates best_fold_state on the LAST fold's loop-leaked X_val/y_val/eff_batch_size (672-687). Pruner steps interleave folds (613), freezing optuna's last_step at fold-0 values.
findings.impact: Composite scores are incomparable across trials with different forward_bars/threshold; serial correlation inflates all Sharpes; the regime penalty is noise; pruning is mostly inert during folds 1-2.
findings.recommendation: Simulate non-overlapping holds (enter, hold fb bars, skip intervening signals) or shrink by effective sample size; annualize crypto with 8760 bars/year; label regimes from 1-bar returns; run the regime check on the winning fold's own val data.

findings.title: Weekly Saturday retrain never re-harvests — models retrain on frozen, aging data
findings.evidence: Weekly retrain builds phases with _build_harvest_phases(not force_harvest, ...) where force_harvest is True only when a Target_Return_{max_fb} column is missing (run_pipeline.py:1069-1094). The module docstring promises 'Every Saturday 2 AM: re-harvest data + retrain' (run_pipeline.py:8). Manual GUI retrains do harvest (943), subject to a 24h-freshness skip (543-557).
findings.impact: Each weekly cycle reruns Optuna on identical stale data, so the only way to beat the save gate is to overfit the same leaky folds harder; deployed models drift months behind the live market.
findings.recommendation: Pass skip_harvest=False for weekly retrains (harvest is incremental and cheap), or force harvest whenever training-data age exceeds ~6 days.

findings.title: Daily_Sentiment training feature contains look-ahead: FnG shifted one day into the future and intraday article aggregation
findings.evidence: alternative.me FnG timestamps are midnight UTC; sentiment_history.py:232 buckets them with datetime.date.fromtimestamp (LOCAL tz), so on a US-timezone Jetson day D's value is stored under D-1; harvest then maps it onto UTC bar dates (harvest_crypto_data.py:181-183) — every crypto bar gets the NEXT day's index value. For stocks, the daily score averages ALL articles dated D (sentiment_history.py:123-168) onto every hourly bar of D (harvest_stock_data.py:175-178); article dates also use local fromtimestamp (406).
findings.impact: A feature carrying up to 24h of future information inflates train/val fit and feature importance; live inference supplies only point-in-time values, so the learned dependence breaks at serving.
findings.recommendation: Bucket with fromtimestamp(ts, tz=timezone.utc); attribute FnG published at 00:00 UTC of day D to day D's bars; for stocks attach only articles timestamped before each bar, or lag the daily score one day.

findings.title: Stock Daily_Sentiment never refreshes after the first fetch and is constant/zero at inference
findings.evidence: fetch_stock_sentiment_history skips any ticker with >=1 article anywhere in the 365-day window (sentiment_history.py:327-334), so new dates are never fetched for ~a year. Harvest uses cached_only=True (harvest_stock_data.py:173-174) defaulting 0.0; get_live_daily_sentiment reads only today's (missing) row -> 0.0 for stocks (sentiment_history.py:491-495). predict_now.py:184-188 injects one constant across the whole seq_len window, whereas training had per-day-varying values.
findings.impact: Training data has real sentiment for old history then zeros afterward — a regime artifact the LSTM can latch onto — and the feature is dead live for stocks: systematic train/serve skew.
findings.recommendation: Fetch missing date ranges per ticker (latest cached date through today) instead of skip-if-any-articles, and run --fetch-stocks before each harvest. At inference, fill the window with each bar's actual historical daily value.

findings.title: Model/scaler/config/features saved as four non-atomic writes; hot reload keys on .pth mtime alone
findings.evidence: hypersearch writes model_v2.pth first, then config/scaler/feature_cols pickles directly to final paths (hypersearch_v2.py:911-929). Bots poll only the .pth mtime and reload all four (base_loop.py:289-303); a reload between writes pairs new weights with the old scaler/config — if tensor shapes match, the load succeeds, model_mtime is advanced (300), and the mismatch persists until the next save. Pipeline retrains stop bots first (run_pipeline.py:1121), so the race applies to manual hypersearch runs while bots trade.
findings.impact: Silently mis-scaled features and wrong threshold/seq_len in a live money path after a manual retrain; torn .pth reads merely retry harmlessly.
findings.recommendation: Write all artifacts to a temp dir and os.replace() each, saving a manifest (or the .pth) LAST and polling that file; better, bundle scaler stats + config into the checkpoint so the artifact set is one atomic file.

findings.title: Optuna study and adaptive best_score ratchet persist across retrains with changing data and label definitions
findings.evidence: create_study(load_if_exists=True) on {prefix}v2_study.db (hypersearch_v2.py:848-856); prior trials seed the score new trials must beat (871-879); adaptive best_score only increases (adaptive_config.py:293-302) and gates model saving (hypersearch_v2.py:896-899). The DB is deleted only on categorical expansion (adaptive_config.py:318-323), after which TPE/pruner need 60 startup trials (PRUNE_STARTUP_TRIALS=60) versus refine runs of 70 trials (TRIAL_COUNTS).
findings.impact: TPE conditions on scores from older data vintages/label sets; a lucky leak-inflated historical score can make the save gate permanently unbeatable, freezing the deployed model; post-reset cycles are ~86% random sampling with no pruning.
findings.recommendation: Store a dataset hash in adaptive state and reset best_score plus the study (--fresh) when it changes; decay best_score per cycle (e.g., x0.95); drop n_startup_trials to ~20 for 70-trial refine runs.

findings.title: Each harvest run permanently erodes ~100 oldest bars per ticker
findings.evidence: Harvest saves post-dropna featured rows (harvest_crypto_data.py:123) and incremental runs rebuild OHLCV from previously SAVED rows (139-158), refetching only latest-48h (61-73). Recomputing indicators over that frame leaves its first ~100 rows (SMA_100/Hurst warmup) NaN again, which dropna removes — the raw bars preceding the saved head no longer exist to rewarm them. Same pattern in harvest_stock_data.py:90-118.
findings.impact: ~100 bars of the oldest history are silently lost per ticker per harvest run; frequent manual retrains compound into months of vanished training history.
findings.recommendation: Persist raw OHLCV in a separate parquet (pre-dropna) and recompute features from that full raw history each harvest; only the featured training file should be warmup-trimmed.

audits.overall:
The README/task premise is stale: there are no dual bear/bull classifiers or bull_threshold. The v2 system is a single RegressionLSTM predicting fb-bar percent returns, gated by an Optuna-tuned trade_threshold — that inference formula itself (predicted return vs threshold, confidence = pred/threshold) is sane. model_lgb.py is dead code: train_lgb/save_lgb_model are never called, so predict_now's lazy ensemble load always finds no file.

Genuine strengths: (1) within-fold RobustScaler is fit strictly on train-index rows — no scaler leakage — and the saved scaler matches the saved weights; (2) sequence windows never cross ticker boundaries and the label bar is excluded from its own window; (3) indicators are all trailing-window (no centered or full-series statistics), with careful Numba kernels matching pandas semantics; (4) inference selects features by name from feature_cols.pkl (column order/presence cannot silently skew; mismatch fails loudly to None) and JIT tracing is done correctly — eval() before trace, fixed shape matching the actual input, eager fallback; (5) training data and adaptive state use atomic tmp+os.replace writes, and the OOM-aware batch-halving training loop is well adapted to the 8GB Jetson.

The dominant problems are structural: the 'walk-forward' split is actually a cross-symbol split sharing calendar time, the Sharpe objective is incomparable across trials and inflated by overlapping trades, the crypto live path cannot supply enough fresh bars for the tuned seq_len, the stock dataset mixes two bar grids and adjustment conventions, and sentiment features leak up to a day of future information while being stale or constant at serving. Fixing the split, the objective simulator, and the live bar fetch would change real-world results more than any model architecture work.

findings.title: Stale-score check collapses 600s analyst interval to ~60s, exhausting daily budget then disabling LLM
findings.evidence: _check_llm_staleness (base_loop.py:497-512) takes the OLDEST timestamp across ALL symbols in the llm_analysis.json section and sets _last_llm_time=0 when >2h. But _save_analysis only updates current candidates (llm_analyst.py:132-142): the stock loop refreshes its top-10 while the section holds ~57 symbols from refresh-all, so non-candidates go stale permanently. Once tripped, analyze_trades runs every other 30s cycle. Failures also retry every cycle (base_loop.py:479-481).
findings.impact: ~390 analyst calls/day vs 39 intended; routing demotes to flash-lite within hours, then the $1 cap (llm_client.py:431) silently disables ALL LLM calls — gating runs on morning-stale scores while each call stalls the trading cycle 5-30s.
findings.recommendation: Track staleness per-candidate: refresh only when max(timestamp of current candidates) > 2h, or stamp a section-level last_refresh key. Keep a separate failure backoff (e.g., 120s exponential) instead of retrying every 30s cycle. Log when scores in use exceed LLM_INTERVAL_SEC age.

findings.title: No schema-enforced output; json_mode silently disabled for the default analyst model on a false premise
findings.evidence: generationConfig carries only maxOutputTokens — temperature is never set (llm_client.py:630-637, Gemini 2.5 default 1.0). json_mode adds responseMimeType only when 'pro' not in model (631-633, comment 'not supported by thinking models' is incorrect — 2.5 Pro supports it, plus responseSchema). Paid routing assigns analyst=gemini-2.5-pro (:100), so the JSON-critical call runs unforced; the call_llm fallback has no json_mode at all (llm_analyst.py:95-96). Result: 130 lines of fence-stripping/brace-counting/truncation-repair/array-fix parsers (llm_analyst.py:391-519) and repeated bugfix commits (34b1daa, ff872b7).
findings.impact: Free-text JSON intermittently fails to parse → symbols drop to default s=0.5 (1.0x, no veto); whole responses discarded; nondeterministic scoring at temperature 1.0 makes the gate noisy.
findings.recommendation: Use Gemini responseSchema (or Anthropic output_config json_schema if migrating): {SYMBOL: {s: number, bull: string, bear: string, r: string}} with propertyOrdering; set temperature 0.1-0.3 for analyst and sentiment roles. Delete the repair-parser stack. Apply json_mode to ALL models including pro and to the fallback path.

findings.title: Analyst routed to 2.5 Pro with 15s timeout and thinking-inclusive 4096-token cap; falls back silently and mis-attributes the model
findings.evidence: Routing picks gemini-2.5-pro for analyst below $0.10/day (llm_client.py:100); per-request timeout = max_llm_latency_sec default 15 (llm_config.py:24, llm_client.py:453). Pro is a thinking model — a 10-candidate analysis routinely exceeds 15s, and thinking tokens count against maxOutputTokens=max(4096,n*400) (llm_analyst.py:89), so responses finish MAX_TOKENS and are discarded (llm_client.py:659-661; commit ff872b7). analyze_trades then calls call_llm → configured gemini-2.5-flash-lite, but _save_analysis records model=analyst_model (llm_analyst.py:104,124-148) — the pro name.
findings.impact: Most analyst calls burn 15s on a doomed pro attempt, then score with flash-lite without JSON mode; GUI and llm_analysis.json claim pro produced the scores. Silent model switching is never journaled, so scoring-behavior changes mid-session are invisible.
findings.recommendation: Route the pre-trade gate to flash/flash-lite (or claude-haiku-4-5, $1/$5/MTok) — fast, schema-capable, adequate for a sizing gate. If keeping pro, set thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget, raise maxOutputTokens to ~8192, and timeout to 45s (the 600s interval affords it). Return (text, model_used) from call paths and persist the actual responder.

findings.title: Fallback chain never fires on the most common failures (timeouts, truncation, safety blocks); chain aborts on empty result
findings.evidence: call_llm reaches the chain only via HTTPError in _FALLBACK_CODES or unresolved 429 (llm_client.py:535-565); generic exceptions including socket timeouts 'return None' (557-560), and a None from _call_gemini (MAX_TOKENS discard, safety block, empty parts) is returned directly at 534 — the comment 'caller will retry via fallback' (661) is false. _try_gemini_chain likewise does 'return result' even when result is None (576-581), aborting remaining models.
findings.impact: Given the 15s timeout, the dominant failure mode (timeout) gets zero fallback: the cycle stalls then trades at default s=0.5 with no veto capability, while the README-advertised lite-fallback chain rarely executes.
findings.recommendation: Treat None/timeout/truncation identically to 5xx: continue the chain (`if result: return result; continue`). Catch socket.timeout/URLError in call_llm and fall through to _try_gemini_chain. Log a structured 'llm_fallback' journal event with from_model/to_model/reason so mid-session behavior shifts are auditable.

findings.title: No measurement loop: journal is write-only and its single LLM metric counts a key that is never written
findings.evidence: get_journal_summary counts skip_reason=='llm_block' (trade_journal.py:67) but writers emit 'llm_veto' (base_loop.py:823, stock_loop.py:380) — llm_blocks is permanently 0. Repo-wide grep shows get_journal_summary has zero callers. 'llm_multiplier' mixes semantics: raw s on skips (base_loop.py:825) vs 0.5+s on buys (:898), corrupting avg_multiplier. Nothing anywhere computes vetoed-trade counterfactuals or s-vs-P&L correlation.
findings.impact: The system spends money and applies 0.65-1.5x sizing plus forced veto-sells with zero evidence the LLM improves P&L; miscalibration (e.g., scores inversely correlated with returns) would never be detected.
findings.recommendation: Fix the key ('llm_veto') and log s and 0.5+s as separate fields. Add an eval job: journal every candidate (s, pred, taken, mid-quote); at position close or T+forward_bars fetch bars and record realized/counterfactual return; weekly, bucket by s-decile and compare taken vs vetoed and (0.5+s)-sized vs flat-sized P&L. Surface uplift in the GUI Models tab.

findings.title: Prompt omits the score's consequences, per-symbol position state, and promised context; rubric semantics diverge from the action mapping
findings.evidence: The prompt gives per-candidate pred ('ML model prediction: {pred:+.4f}% (bullish signal)'), ≤5 headlines, fundamentals_text, trade-memory lesson (llm_analyst.py:345-379) and a portfolio-level 'Currently holding' line. It never states that s<0.15 blocks buys AND force-sells held positions (base_loop.py:554-581) or that size scales by 0.5+s (:827). Loops never pass fng_value (base_loop.py:474-478) so the 'Market regime' line never renders in-loop; model_config is accepted but unused (llm_analyst.py:311-388). No entry price/P&L, exposure, or cost hurdle per candidate.
findings.impact: An LLM scoring 0.10 on a held position triggers liquidation without knowing it holds; rubric-'Bearish' scores (0.15-0.35) still buy at 0.65-0.85x; labeling pre-filtered top-10 candidates 'bullish signal' invites agreement bias.
findings.recommendation: State the mapping explicitly: 'size = base × (0.5+s); s<0.15 blocks new buys and liquidates the position.' Per candidate, include held qty/entry/unrealized P&L, round-trip cost hurdle (spread×2 + slippage), and current exposure; pass fng_value and remove or use model_config. Either make 0.15-0.35 reduce-to-zero or relabel the band.

findings.title: Filing 'summaries' ask the LLM to invent 10-K/10-Q content from memory, then feed it into trade-gating prompts
findings.evidence: get_filing_summary builds: 'the most recent {form} was filed on {date}. Based on your knowledge... summarize the key risks, guidance changes, and notable items' — explicitly without fetching filing text (fundamentals.py:233-245, comment 'we don't fetch full text'). Output is cached 7 days and injected per top-10 stock candidate via format_fundamentals_for_llm (stock_loop.py:210-213).
findings.impact: 2026 filings post-date Gemini 2.5 training cutoffs, so 'guidance changes' are fabricated and presented to the analyst gate as fact, distorting s scores that size and veto real orders for a week per cache entry.
findings.recommendation: Fetch the actual filing section (EDGAR allows 10 req/s with a UA; pull Item 1A/7 or the 8-K body) and summarize that, or drop the feature. At minimum, reword to 'a {form} was filed on {date}; do not speculate on its contents' so the date is signal without invented specifics.

findings.title: Cost and rate-limit accounting undercounts: chain/retry calls unbilled, thinking tokens invisible, per-process limits multiply ~5x
findings.evidence: _try_gemini_chain successes call record_call but never _record_cost (llm_client.py:576-597); call_gemini's post-429 retry records the call but not cost (474-481). _estimate_cost uses chars/4 of the final text only (365-370) — pro's billed thinking tokens (~$10/MTok output) are invisible. RPM deque and RPD counters are per-process module globals (75-88) across 2 bots + GUI + backfill + refresh subprocesses; only dollars share llm_cost.json. Tier detection reads 'x-ratelimit-limit-requests' (160), a header Gemini does not send, so detection never fires.
findings.impact: The $1.00/day cap is enforced against an undercount — pro thinking alone can add $0.02-0.03 per analyst call unrecorded — and aggregate request rate can reach ~5x the intended 30 RPM, risking 429 storms.
findings.recommendation: Bill from the API's usageMetadata (promptTokenCount, candidatesTokenCount, thoughtsTokenCount) returned in every generateContent response instead of chars/4; record cost on every successful path. Move RPM/RPD counters into the shared llm_cost.json (single writer via os.replace). Delete the header-based tier probe; make tier explicit config.

findings.title: Backfill worker pays full real-time prices instead of Batch API at 50%, only runs during retrain due to inverted live_mode, and has a Python 3.10 crash path
findings.evidence: run_backfill_worker scores 50-article batches via synchronous tiered call_gemini at 8 RPM (sentiment_history.py:535-628) — latency-irrelevant work ideal for Gemini's Batch API (50% off; Anthropic Batches equivalent). set_live_mode(True) at bot launch (run_pipeline.py:873-874) pauses it ~permanently (crypto runs 24/7); the 'Pause backfill during retrain' comment calls set_live_mode(False) which RESUMES it during training (run_pipeline.py:1038-1040). _fetch_full_texts catches builtins TimeoutError (sentiment.py:610-616), which on the Jetson's Python 3.10 does not catch concurrent.futures.TimeoutError; _llm_score_batch (sentiment_history.py:596) has no try, so the worker process dies.
findings.impact: Historical Daily_Sentiment (a training feature) backfills only during Saturday retrain windows — competing for unified memory and LLM quota exactly when training needs both — at double the necessary cost, and can crash outright on a slow article fetch.
findings.recommendation: Submit unscored articles as Gemini Batch jobs (flash-lite batch: $0.0375/$0.15 per MTok — ~10k articles ≈ $0.15 one-off) on a daily cron; poll results. Fix the flag: backfill should run while live (it's why max_rpm=8 leaves headroom) and pause during training. Catch concurrent.futures.TimeoutError explicitly.

findings.title: llm_analysis.json written by 4 processes with unlocked non-atomic read-modify-write; GUI refresh subprocesses risk pipe deadlock and code injection
findings.evidence: _save_analysis does load → mutate → open('w')+json.dump with no lock or tmp/rename (llm_analyst.py:124-148); writers: crypto bot, stock bot, GUI refresh_one and refresh-all subprocesses. Readers swallow JSONDecodeError returning {} (109-121). GUI spawns subprocesses with stdout=PIPE that is never drained (gui.py:2595-2606, 2658-2668; 'count symbols done' unimplemented at 2682) and f-string-injects the symbol into python -c (2596-2597); interpreter path hardcoded (2585, 2647).
findings.impact: Concurrent writes lose a section or tear the file — bots then load {} and trade at s=0.5 with no veto until the next refresh; a chatty refresh-all can fill the 64KB pipe and hang forever with the button disabled; a malformed universe symbol breaks or executes code.
findings.recommendation: Write via tmp+os.replace under an fcntl.flock (pattern already used for llm_cost.json); merge per-section. Drain subprocess output (stdout=DEVNULL or a reader thread) and pass the symbol as argv to a real CLI entrypoint (llm_analyst.py --refresh-one SYM), not interpolated -c code.

findings.title: Gemini 3.x half-migration: GUI offers 3.x models that routing silently ignores and the budget panel reports fictitious quotas
findings.evidence: Settings dropdowns offer gemini-3.1-pro-preview / gemini-3-flash-preview / gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview (gui.py:3382-3389, 3402-3408) saved as overrides, but get_recommended_model honors an override only if it is in the 2.5-only GEMINI_MODELS list (llm_client.py:216-217) — selections are saved then ignored without any message. The Models-tab panel queries get_budget for the 3.x names (gui.py:4658-4661), which always returns the default (50,50) since calls record under 2.5 names; the news-upgrade filter compares to never-assigned 'gemini-3.1-pro-preview' (gui.py:963).
findings.impact: User's explicit model choice does nothing; the usage dashboard shows static fake budgets while real consumption is invisible — by June 2026 the system is pinned to legacy 2.5 models with no working upgrade path.
findings.recommendation: Drive GEMINI_MODELS, _PRICING, budgets, and the GUI dropdowns from one model registry; validate overrides on save and surface 'override not supported' in the GUI. Add the 3.x family (or current equivalents) to the registry with pricing before listing them.

findings.title: GUI news loop perpetually re-scores display articles toward gemini-2.5-pro, draining the shared trade budget
findings.evidence: Every 300s fetch_news tick, articles whose _scored_by_model != 'gemini-3.1-pro-preview' (a name never assigned; gui.py:961-963) are passed to try_llm_upgrade, which re-scores up to 10 toward gemini-2.5-pro whenever pro has RPD budget (sentiment.py:779-788). These scores color the news table only; cost lands in the same shared llm_cost.json and $1.00/day cap the trade-path analyst draws from (llm_client.py:373-381).
findings.impact: Up to ~120 article re-scores/hour on the most expensive model for cosmetic display values, accelerating the daily cost cap that then disables pre-trade analysis — display polish directly degrades the money path.
findings.recommendation: Score display news with flash-lite only and stop upgrading (one pass per article); fix the filter to the models actually assigned. Better: partition the daily budget per role (e.g., analyst $0.60, sentiment $0.25, GUI $0.15) inside llm_cost.json so display traffic can never starve the trade gate.

audits.overall:
The LLM layer has genuinely good bones: one batched analyst call per cycle with fail-open semantics (parse failure → s=0.5 pass-through, never blocking trades), cross-process daily cost sharing via atomic llm_cost.json with midnight-PT reset, tiered spend-aware model routing with per-model RPD budgets and 429 retry-after parsing, an anti-0.50-anchoring rubric that is real prompt craft, and trade_memory lessons fed back into prompts. API keys are plaintext but correctly gitignored (.gitignore:42); the non-atomic llm_config.json written concurrently by GUI autosave and bots remains a minor clobber risk.

But the system cannot currently tell whether any of it works: the journal is write-only (get_journal_summary has zero callers and counts a skip_reason that is never written), so $-spend and 0.65-1.5x sizing decisions are unvalidated. Despite 'multi-provider' branding (README:386), only Gemini is implemented; Claude/OpenAI are dead config. The single biggest root cause is the absence of structured outputs — json_mode is disabled exactly for the default pro analyst, producing the documented whack-a-mole of parser fixes — compounded by a 15s timeout that dooms the pro call and silently demotes scoring to flash-lite while recording 'pro' as the author.

Redesign: analyst gate on gemini-2.5/3-flash-lite (or claude-haiku-4-5) with responseSchema, temperature 0.2, 30s timeout, per-candidate staleness; sentiment on flash-lite; backfill via Batch API (~50% off, ~$0.15 per 10k articles); bill from usageMetadata; shared RPM ledger; weekly s-decile counterfactual eval. At intended volumes (~183 analyst calls/day) flash-lite costs ~$0.11/day — the $1 cap becomes headroom instead of a ceiling.

Execution-safety audit of the order/state layer. Genuine strengths: (1) buy fills are properly confirmed — manage_order_lifecycle polls status and _place_and_track_buy re-reads qty/avg_entry_price via verify_position, so tracking reflects real fee-adjusted fills; (2) gpu_lock.py uses kernel flock, which auto-releases on process death — no stale-lock hazard; (3) hard-stop lockouts are persisted atomically and the circuit-breaker baseline (Alpaca last_equity) is server-side, so both survive restarts; (4) crypto correctly uses gtc-only TIF and never attempts brackets (unsupported on Alpaca crypto), and stock _execute_sells correctly cancels the stop leg before selling. However, the system has three critical correctness bugs in money paths: the 3:50pm flatten silently fails for every position whose bracket/trailing leg still holds the shares (then sets flattened_today, guaranteeing overnight gap exposure); the software-stop handler misclassifies the same shares-reserved rejection as a broker desync and deletes real positions from tracking; and the crypto loop fails open on missing predictions — buying the whole universe with zero model gating if the model file is absent, and liquidating positions on transient data failures. Order handling lacks idempotency (no client_order_id) and the market fallback re-submits the full original qty after partial fills. Stops are client-side-only for crypto (24/7) and stock server-side stops are permanently stripped after any restart because startup cancels all account orders and reconstruction never re-places them. The deprecated alpaca-trade-api SDK is REST-polling only. Fix the flatten/desync/None-prediction trio before going live.

findings.title: EOD flatten fails for every bracket-protected position; no retry, no early-close calendar
findings.evidence: flatten_before_close (stock_loop.py:141-181) sells without canceling info.stop_order_id, unlike _execute_sells which cancels first (stock_loop.py:280-284). Open bracket stop/TP or trailing legs reserve the shares, so Alpaca rejects the sell ('available: 0'); place_stock_limit_order swallows it returning None (order_utils.py:139-141), the position stays, and flattened_today=True is set unconditionally (stock_loop.py:180). check_market_hours hardcodes 16:00 with no get_clock/get_calendar (stock_loop.py:80-91; repo grep: zero calendar usage).
findings.impact: Positions still holding server-side legs at 15:50 are carried overnight with day-TIF legs expiring at 16:00 — unprotected gap risk on up to $50k nightly. On 1pm early-close days the flatten window never arrives at all.
findings.recommendation: Before selling: cancel stop_order_id (and verify cancellation) exactly as _execute_sells does, or call Alpaca's close_position endpoint after cancel_all for the symbol. Only delete positions and set flattened_today after confirming fills; retry failures each cycle within the window. Gate market hours and flatten time on api.get_clock()/get_calendar() instead of hardcoded 16:00.

findings.title: Shares-reserved sell rejection misclassified as desync — real position deleted from tracking
findings.evidence: base _manage_stops runs for stocks via super() (stock_loop.py:519). When the software stop fires it market-sells without canceling the server-side leg (base_loop.py:386-389); macro stop_mult<1 tightens only the software stop (base_loop.py:367-369), placing it above the bracket stop so this path triggers first in stressed regimes. Alpaca rejects ('insufficient qty'/'available: 0' — shares reserved by the open leg), and the handler treats exactly those strings as position-gone, deleting self.positions[symbol] (base_loop.py:404-420).
findings.impact: A live position becomes invisible to the bot: skipped by flatten, sells, and stop management; its day-TIF legs expire at close, leaving untracked unprotected shares overnight until the next process restart resyncs.
findings.recommendation: Cancel pos.stop_order_id before the stop market-sell (mirror stock_loop.py:280-284). In the error handler, verify via api.get_position(symbol) before deleting tracking; only remove on confirmed zero qty. Add a periodic broker-vs-local reconciliation that adopts unknown broker positions into tracking.

findings.title: Crypto loop fails open on missing predictions: buys ungated, sells on transient data failures
findings.evidence: In _execute_buys both should_trade and the threshold gate sit inside 'if pred_return is not None and quote is not None' (base_loop.py:766-770), so pred=None proceeds to buy. With model files missing, the bot logs 'Running without prediction gating' (base_loop.py:221-222) and buys all 6 crypto symbols on sentiment/LLM alone. _execute_sells treats pred=None as a sell signal ('no prediction', base_loop.py:534-541). get_live_prediction returns None on any data hiccup (predict_now.py:152-194). Stock loop overrides both safely (stock_loop.py:262-265, 323).
findings.impact: A torn/missing model file deploys capital with zero model gating; any Alpaca 429 or data outage (likely: ~50 bar fetches per 30s stock cycle plus crypto plus GUI vs 200 req/min) liquidates held crypto, then rebuys after 60-min cooldown — repeated spread/slippage bleed.
findings.recommendation: Fail closed: in _execute_buys skip when pred_return is None; refuse to start trading with model=None. In _execute_sells, require N consecutive None cycles (e.g. 10) before treating missing predictions as actionable, and log a data-outage alert instead of selling on the first failure.

findings.title: Market fallback re-submits original full qty after partial fills; no client_order_id idempotency
findings.evidence: manage_order_lifecycle caches saved_qty = order.qty (requested, not remaining) on first poll (order_utils.py:170-173). After timeout it cancels and submits a market order for saved_qty (order_utils.py:199-208), ignoring filled_qty of the canceled limit. No client_order_id appears anywhere in the repo (grep), and submit_order exceptions return None (order_utils.py:113-115) with no later reconciliation — an order placed during a network timeout fills untracked.
findings.impact: A partially-filled buy plus full-qty market fallback yields up to 2x intended exposure per order. Oversized sells are rejected, leaving remainders unsold with stale tracked qty. Timed-out submits can create untracked, stop-unprotected positions.
findings.recommendation: Compute remaining = float(order.qty) - float(order.filled_qty) after the post-cancel re-fetch and submit the fallback for remaining only. Pass a deterministic client_order_id (e.g. f'{symbol}-{cycle}-{side}') to every submit_order so ambiguous failures can be queried via get_order_by_client_order_id instead of resubmitted blind.

findings.title: Startup cancel-all is account-wide and server-side stops are never re-placed after restart
findings.evidence: run() calls cancel_all_open_orders at startup (base_loop.py:149), which executes api.cancel_all_orders() account-wide (order_utils.py:274-285). Both bots share one account; run_pipeline auto-restarts a crashed bot in ~60s, so a crypto crash cancels every stock bracket/trailing leg mid-day. Reconstruction sets stop_order_id=None (order_utils.py:310) and never re-places a stop; the trailing upgrade requires an existing stop_order_id (stock_loop.py:498-500). HWM also resets to max(entry,current) (order_utils.py:309) and cooldown timers are in-memory only.
findings.impact: After any restart of either bot, all stock positions permanently lose server-side protection (30s software polling only, dependent on process survival), trailing stops loosen, and cooldowns reset allowing immediate re-trades.
findings.recommendation: Cancel only this bot's own orders (filter list_orders by tracked symbols/client_order_id prefix) instead of cancel_all_orders. In _reconstruct_positions, re-submit a stop order per reconstructed stock position and store its id. Persist high_water_mark and last_trade_time alongside hard_stop_lockout.json.

findings.title: Position sizing multiplier stack is unclamped for new positions (~32x base possible)
findings.evidence: _compute_position_size chains Kelly up to 3x base (trading_utils.py:187) x confidence 2.0 (base_loop.py:619) x GARCH 2.0 (volatility.py:148) x HMM 1.2, then gates multiply sentiment up to 1.5 (sentiment.py:1172) and LLM up to 1.5 (base_loop.py:827-828) — ~32x with no final clamp. MAX_NOTIONAL_PER_SYMBOL is checked only when the symbol is already held (base_loop.py:749-752); stock MAX_EXPOSURE is checked before the order but never caps a single order's size (stock_loop.py:312-314); crypto has no total-exposure cap.
findings.impact: A realistic stack (3x2x2x1.35) puts a single new stock order at $80k+ against a $5k intent and $50k exposure cap; crypto can reach ~$32k per order with no portfolio cap, concentrating the account in one fill.
findings.recommendation: Clamp the final figure: sized = min(sized, self.MAX_NOTIONAL_PER_SYMBOL - existing_value) for all entries, and for stocks also min(sized, self.MAX_EXPOSURE - current_exposure). Add a crypto total-exposure cap mirroring MAX_EXPOSURE.

findings.title: Crypto stops are client-side only; process/host death leaves 24/7 positions with no resting protection
findings.evidence: Crypto buys are plain limit orders (crypto_loop.py:67-73, order_utils.py:88-115) — correctly avoiding brackets (unsupported on Alpaca crypto) — but hard stop/trailing/TP exist only as 30s in-process checks (base_loop.py:343-420). No resting stop/stop_limit order is ever placed for crypto. run_pipeline restarts crashed bots in ~60s, but a run_pipeline death, Jetson reboot, power loss, or the 3600s circuit-breaker sleep (base_loop.py:285) leaves positions unmanaged.
findings.impact: Up to ~$18k of crypto (6 symbols x $3k cap; more given the sizing finding) can sit unprotected through overnight/weekend crashes — the exact scenario stops exist for. The 1-hour breaker sleep also suspends stop checking on any surviving positions.
findings.recommendation: Place a resting GTC stop_limit sell on Alpaca for each crypto position at the computed hard-stop price (Alpaca crypto supports stop_limit), updating it when trailing tightens; keep the software layer for TP/trailing. Alternatively run a minimal watchdog (systemd) that flattens crypto if the bot heartbeat goes stale.

findings.title: Uncaught exceptions kill bot processes: None-exposure TypeError and zero-quote ZeroDivisionError; run() has no cycle guard
findings.evidence: After a fill, current_exposure = self._get_current_exposure() (stock_loop.py:458) returns None on API error (stock_loop.py:521-530, order_utils.py:249-256); line 459 evaluates 'None > self.MAX_EXPOSURE' — TypeError. place_limit_order computes qty = notional/limit_price outside its try (order_utils.py:94-95); a degenerate bid=ask=0 quote yields limit_price 0.0 and ZeroDivisionError. run()'s cycle body (base_loop.py:153-208) has no try/except, so either exception kills the process.
findings.impact: One API blip immediately after a fill crashes the stock bot with a fresh position open; the ~60s auto-restart then triggers the account-wide cancel-all cascade (stripping every bracket leg), compounding the damage.
findings.recommendation: Guard None: 'if current_exposure is None or current_exposure > self.MAX_EXPOSURE: break'. Move the qty computation inside the try and reject quotes with midpoint <= 0 in get_quote. Wrap the run() cycle body in try/except Exception with logging so a single-cycle failure never kills the process.

findings.title: Circuit breaker flattens the entire shared account from either bot and fails open on API errors
findings.evidence: check_circuit_breaker uses (last_equity - equity)/last_equity >= 5% — drawdown from previous close, server-side baseline that survives restarts (order_utils.py:321-332) — but returns (False, 0.0) on any API error (order_utils.py:333-335). On trip, emergency_flatten cancels ALL account orders and market-sells ALL positions (order_utils.py:340-367) including the sibling bot's, without verifying fills; the tripped bot clears tracking and sleeps 3600s in-line (base_loop.py:282-285), re-tripping hourly against the static baseline.
findings.impact: A stock drawdown trip liquidates crypto positions (and vice versa), desyncing the other bot's tracking into error churn; flatten failures (rejected/unfilled sells) are silently abandoned; API outages disable the breaker entirely.
findings.recommendation: Scope flatten to the bot's own asset class (filter list_positions by '/' or symbol set). Verify each flatten sell filled and retry failures before declaring halted. Treat repeated check failures as a soft halt (no new buys) rather than fail-open. Replace sleep(3600) with a halted flag so stop management keeps running.

findings.title: Stop/veto exits unconfirmed and journaled at quote midpoint — corrupts Kelly sizing inputs
