findings.evidence: _manage_stops submits a market sell, then immediately record_trade(...) at the quote midpoint and deletes the position without polling for fill or reading filled_avg_price (base_loop.py:386-397). _execute_llm_veto_sells records pnl from the pre-trade quote (base_loop.py:570-578); crypto place_sell_order with quote=None returns True right after submit (crypto_loop.py:89-94). compute_kelly_fraction sizes positions from these pnl_pct values (trading_utils.py:148-166).
findings.impact: Stop exits — precisely the trades with worst slippage (gaps, thin crypto books) — are recorded at optimistic pre-slippage prices, inflating avg_win/avg_loss and the Kelly fraction, which then scales real position sizes up to 3x. Unfilled/rejected exits can also be recorded as done.
findings.recommendation: Poll the stop sell to terminal status (reuse manage_order_lifecycle) and journal filled_avg_price/filled_qty; only delete the position on confirmed fill. Where confirmation is unavailable, mark the trade record estimated and exclude estimated records from compute_kelly_fraction.

findings.title: Sentiment and LLM gates fail open; documented news hard-block does not exist
findings.evidence: sentiment_gate clamps to max(0.15, min(1.5, m)) (sentiment.py:1172-1174), so the 'gate <= 0' skip branches are unreachable dead code (base_loop.py:811, stock_loop.py:368) — README's 'symbol news <= -0.3 blocks trades' is false (it only scales to 0.35x/0.15x). On news-fetch failure the component is skipped at neutral 1.0. analyze_trades returns {} on any LLM failure (llm_analyst.py:96-98) and absent symbols default s=0.5 → 1.0x with no veto (base_loop.py:820).
findings.impact: When Finnhub/Gemini are down or rate-limited, the bot silently trades at full size with no news veto and no LLM veto — the advertised last-line risk filters provide zero protection exactly during outages, and operators believe a block exists that doesn't.
findings.recommendation: Decide intent explicitly: if fail-open is desired, fix the README and delete the dead gate<=0 branches; if not, return a sentinel (None) from sentiment_gate/analyze_trades on data failure and reduce size (e.g. 0.5x) or skip new entries when both signals are unavailable. Implement a true block for scores <= -0.5 if catastrophic-news blocking is intended.

findings.title: Deprecated alpaca-trade-api SDK (REST polling only) — unmaintained since 2023
findings.evidence: All broker access goes through tradeapi.REST (trading_utils.py:14,36-41; gui.py:22,4730; requirements.txt 'alpaca-trade-api>=3.0.0'); no websocket/stream usage anywhere (grep). Alpaca deprecated this SDK at end-2022 in favor of alpaca-py — bug patches ended and the repo is in maintenance/archive state (github.com/alpacahq/alpaca-trade-api-python; pypi.org/project/alpaca-trade-api; alpaca.markets blog 'Unveiling Alpaca-py').
findings.impact: No fixes if Alpaca changes endpoints/response fields (crypto endpoints have churned historically); polling-only fill detection underlies the desync and partial-fill findings; dependency pins (aiohttp/websockets) will increasingly conflict on Python upgrades.
findings.recommendation: Plan migration to alpaca-py (TradingClient + TradingStream). Highest-value first step: subscribe to trade_updates via TradingStream so fills/partial fills/cancels arrive as events instead of 2s polling — this directly removes the partial-fill and shares-reserved race classes. Sources: https://github.com/alpacahq/alpaca-trade-api-python , https://pypi.org/project/alpaca-trade-api/ , https://github.com/alpacahq/alpaca-py

verifications.title: No strategy-level backtest; model selection uses an unrealizable trade simulator
verifications.reasoning: Verified compute_sharpe at scripts/hypersearch_v2.py:258-280: per-bar signals each earn the full Target_Return_fb (fb in 12-48; harvest_crypto_data.py:118 / harvest_stock_data.py:113 confirm full forward returns), annualized via sqrt(trade_freq*1638), with 1638 hard-coded ("hourly stock bars/year") for crypto runs too. Repo-wide grep: zero backtest code anywhere; scripts/ holds only harvest+hypersearch. Promotion gate is trial score (hypersearch_v2.py:899); base_loop.py hot-reloads .pth. Live loop is long-only with stops/cooldowns/flatten, so simulated shorts are unrealizable. Mitigations found (walk-forward CV+embargo, regime penalty, 5bps cost, fold-std penalty, MC bootstrap) all sit atop the same overlapping-return metric. Minor nuances only: trade_threshold IS shared with the live entry gate, and 1638-vs-8760 deflates crypto rather than inflates; neither materially weakens the finding.

verifications.title: Walk-forward folds split across tickers, not time — cross-asset leakage; deployed artifact is one fold
verifications.reasoning: Verified in /Users/kywwilson/Desktop/Projects/trader/scripts/hypersearch_v2.py: load_data stacks per-ticker blocks contiguously (lines 177-193); get_walk_forward_folds builds all_valid in ticker order (223-227) and slices positionally at 60/73.3/86.7% (233-246), so 'train' spans the first tickers' full 2021-2026 histories (harvest_crypto_data.py:30-37 — exactly 6 crypto tickers, ALPACA_START 2021-01-01) while 'val' is another ticker's contemporaneous, even calendar-earlier, data; the seq_len positional embargo (219, 238) cannot fix that. Best-fold weights/scaler are cached (654-658, 702-708) and saved unretrained (899-933); run_pipeline.py only re-runs the search; predict_now.py:38-71 + base_loop.py:26 deploy these artifacts live. Aggravator: the last ~13% of rows (~LINK) never appears in any train fold yet is traded.

verifications.title: Crypto edge cannot plausibly clear the real fee hurdle; cost model off ~10x and live gate is fee-blind
verifications.reasoning: Verified every citation. order_utils.py:261-269: should_trade gates only on |pred| > 2*spread_pct, no fee term; called at base_loop.py:767. Entries: mid+5bps limits (order_utils.py:60-115), 30s timeout then market fallback (order_utils.py:199-220; crypto_loop.py:37,67-73). Stop/TP/trailing exits are market (base_loop.py:386-389); circuit-breaker flatten too (order_utils.py:355-365). hypersearch_v2.py:255,274: TRANSACTION_COST_BPS=5 round-trip is the repo's ONLY cost model — grep finds no maker/taker/fee term anywhere, no post-only option, no crypto override. trade_threshold tuned in [0.05,1.0] (hypersearch_v2.py:426-427; adaptive_config.py:29 allows 0.01); live default 0.15% (base_loop.py:82). Targets/predictions are percent returns. Minor nuance: live holds are multi-bar (3:1 TP), so "-0.45%/round trip" mirrors the training one-bar simulation, but the fee-blind conclusion stands.

# Jetson Orin Nano 8GB Deployment Research — trader stack

## 1. PyTorch + CUDA context cost per process (the dominant tax)
**Established:** `import torch` alone costs ~160-170MB RSS (libtorch globals; measured by pytorch-memlab author's analysis); on the aarch64 CUDA-enabled wheel expect ~200-350MB. Touching CUDA is far worse: NVIDIA staff (dusty_nv) confirm the overhead is "compiled CUDA kernel binaries and libraries like cuDNN" loaded per process — a 0.5M-param model historically drove a process to 2GB+ on Jetson. On an Orin Nano running ResNet50, a user measured **2.5GB process usage of which only 1.4GB was GPU-shared** (JetPack 5, pre-lazy-loading); NVIDIA's fix was "upgrade to JetPack 6 for CUDA lazy loading." CUDA 12.2+ (JetPack 6 = CUDA 12.2/12.6) enables `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY` **by default**, but cuDNN/cuBLAS still load on first use — an LSTM forward pulls in cuDNN. **Realistic JP6 estimate: +0.6-1.2GB RSS per process that initializes CUDA, even for a 1.3MB model.** Four CUDA-touching processes would burn 2.5-5GB of your 8GB before any data. Your design already dodges this: `trading_utils.choose_inference_device()` hard-returns `'cpu'` and `gpu_lock.py` serializes training — that is the correct architecture for this board.

**Trap found in your code:** `hw_monitor.is_gpu_available()` allocates `torch.zeros(1, device='cuda')` — calling it from any bot/GUI process permanently creates a ~1GB CUDA context *in that process*. `trading_utils.py:17` imports it. Guard it (env var `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""` in bot environments is a hard guarantee, and cheap).

## 2. GPU vs CPU for your tiny LSTM
**Established:** for small models at batch 1, eager-mode kernel-launch/dispatch overhead is 20-30%+ of step time and CPU dispatch becomes the bottleneck; NVIDIA's own Torch-TensorRT tuning guide says a tiny model at batch 1 is "unlikely to be faster in TRT than eager." A hidden-200 LSTM forward on a GTX 1060 measured ~0.56ms — the same order as CPU for ~300k params. Your RegressionLSTM (2×128 LSTM + MHA + FC ≈ 0.3M params, seq 12-24, batch 1) runs in roughly **0.5-3ms on the Orin's Cortex-A78AE cores** (estimate) — trivially inside a 30s cycle scoring 10-47 symbols. GPU inference would buy nothing and cost ~1GB/process. **Verdict: CPU inference is correct; do not revisit.** Set `torch.set_num_threads(2)` + `OMP_NUM_THREADS=2` in the bots — for tiny RNNs, fewer threads usually beats the default 6-thread spawn and stops the bots stealing cores from training (established PyTorch CPU practice; exact best value needs a 5-min benchmark).

## 3. TensorRT / torch2trt / ONNX Runtime
**Established:** LSTM→TRT is a known pain: ONNX Loop/dynamic-shape handling, torch2trt unsupported ops, and "LSTM + dynamic batch consumes more resources" (NVIDIA forums, TensorRT GitHub). TRT also adds its own runtime+engine memory and a CUDA context — net negative here. **ONNX Runtime CPU is the interesting option:** 2-4x speedups vs PyTorch eager on CPU for small/BiLSTM models are repeatedly reported, the plain `pip install onnxruntime` aarch64 CPU wheel works on Jetson (Python 3.10 tested), and it would let bot processes drop torch entirely (~50-100MB ORT vs 200-350MB torch import). Export with opset≥17 (LayerNorm/MHA support). Effort is moderate; payoff is ~150-300MB/process + lower latency. `torch.jit.trace` on CPU is the zero-effort middle ground but keeps the torch import.

## 4. Training/Optuna limits on 8GB
Your `scripts/hypersearch_v2.py` already has the right mitigations: single-fold sequence cache (~280MB/fold, line 320), OOM-retry halving batch to ≥128, AMP (`torch.amp.autocast`+GradScaler), `gc.collect()`+`empty_cache()`. AMP/fp16 is fully supported on Orin's Ampere SM8.7 tensor cores (established). Remaining issues:
- `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True` (line 83) only affects **convolutions** — your net has none, so it buys nothing and benchmark mode is a documented source of transient workspace OOM spikes. Remove it (zero risk).
- The fold cache materializes dense (N, seq, F) float32 arrays. At 700k rows × seq 24 × 40 features that's ~2.7GB; your comment says ~280MB/fold at current sizes. If row counts grow, switch to gathering `train_indices[:,None]+offsets` **per batch** (2048×24×40×4B ≈ 8MB) instead of per fold — biggest single training-RAM lever.
- GPU-side memory is not the binding constraint (params 0.3M; batch 2048 activations are tens of MB); **host RAM for CUDA binaries + dataset is**. Peak retrain process: ~1.2-2GB CUDA/torch + 0.3-0.6GB data ≈ **2.5-3.5GB** (estimate). With both bots (~0.6-0.9GB each) running through Saturday retrain, you're at ~5-6GB — workable headless, fragile with desktop+GUI. Avoid `pin_memory` for bulk data on unified memory (pinned pages just remove RAM from the shared pool; Orin has I/O coherency so small pinned staging buffers are fine — NVIDIA CUDA-for-Tegra appnote).

## 5. System-level (JetPack 6)
**Established (Jetson AI Lab "RAM Optimization" tutorial + NVIDIA forums):**
- Disabling the Ubuntu desktop frees **~800MB**: `sudo systemctl set-default multi-user.target`. Biggest free win available.
- Default nvzramconfig zram ≈ 50% of RAM (~3.7GB compressed, costs CPU). Standard recommendation for 8GB boards doing ML: `sudo systemctl disable nvzramconfig`, create 8-16GB swap on NVMe (`fallocate`/`mkswap`/`swapon` + fstab), set `vm.swappiness≈10-20` so swap is a crash-net, not a working set. dusty_nv: CUDA binary pages "swap out well."
- JetPack 6.2 "Super" modes for Orin Nano: new 25W and uncapped MAXN SUPER (GPU 1020MHz, mem 3200MHz → 102GB/s), up to ~1.7-2x throughput (NVIDIA blog). 25W is the perf/W sweet spot per 2026 benchmarks. Use `nvpmodel -m <25W/MAXN SUPER>` + `jetson_clocks` only during the retrain window (you already have `wait_for_cool_gpu`); 15W or 7W suffices for bot inference.
- Monitoring: `pip install jetson-stats` → `jtop` (Orin-supported, importable Python API — could replace parts of `hw_monitor.py`); `tegrastats --interval 5000` for logging during retrain.

## 6. GUI
PySide6 idle apps measure ~215-220MB RSS (Vorta datapoint); your 199KB dashboard with pyqtgraph heatmaps will sit ~300-500MB (estimate), **plus** ~800MB desktop stack if rendered on the Jetson. A FastAPI/uvicorn JSON+static dashboard runs ~120-140MB (Flask ~54MB) and the browser cost moves to another machine: **net ~1.0-1.3GB reclaimed** if the Jetson currently renders gui.py locally. If gui.py already runs on your desktop via Alpaca API (it has no Jetson-only deps), this item is moot — verify.

## 7. Numba on aarch64
Numba officially lists aarch64 as supported-but-lower-tier (historically built/tested on Jetson TX2). Your `@njit(cache=True)` in indicators.py is correct. First-call JIT of ~20-40 kernels on Orin will take tens of seconds to a few minutes total (estimate); with cache=True it's once per code/numba/python change. Gotchas (numba docs): cache is invalidated by numba/Python upgrades; the source directory must be writable (`__pycache__`); run a one-shot warmup at deploy so the first trading cycle isn't slow. Don't switch to AOT — not worth it.

## 8. PyTorch 2.8.0 jetson-ai-lab wheels
**Established (NVIDIA forums #346195, #341339):** the `pypi.jetson-ai-lab.io/jp6/cu126` torch 2.8.0 wheel imports fail with `ImportError: libcudss.so.0` on stock JetPack 6.2; NVIDIA's fix is installing **cuDSS 0.7.1 (aarch64-jetson, Ubuntu 22.04)** from developer.nvidia.com. cuSPARSELt is likewise required by 2024+ builds (docs.pytorch.org Jetson page): install to `/usr/local/cuda/lib64` + `sudo ldconfig`. **Best practice: system-install + ldconfig, not per-shell LD_LIBRARY_PATH** — your bots are spawned by `run_pipeline.py` and systemd/cron environments won't inherit shell exports (a classic "works in terminal, dies under systemd" failure).

## 9. Multi-process GPU architecture
CUDA MPS is now supported on Jetson (JetPack 6.1+/CUDA 12.5 — CUDA-for-Tegra appnote), and Triton runs on Jetson (NVIDIA recommends the in-process C API at the edge; CUDA IPC unsupported). But both exist to share a GPU among processes that *need* it. Your workload doesn't: one CUDA context total (the trainer, gated by `gpu_lock`) + CPU inference everywhere else is the right answer and simpler than MPS/Triton. If you ever need GPU inference, run ONE inference daemon over a unix socket rather than per-bot contexts.

## 10. Memory budget (estimates; verify with `smem`/jtop)
| Component | Now | After recommendations |
|---|---|---|
| OS headless base | ~0.7-0.9GB | same |
| Desktop GUI stack | ~0.8GB | **0 (headless)** |
| gui.py (PySide6+pyqtgraph) | ~0.3-0.5GB | 0 on-device (web/remote) |
| crypto_loop (torch CPU) | ~0.6-0.9GB | ~0.4-0.6GB (ORT, 1 merged bot) |
| stock_loop | ~0.6-0.9GB | merged |
| run_pipeline parent | ~0.1GB | same |
| Weekly retrain peak | ~2.5-3.5GB | ~2.2-3GB |
| **Worst-case concurrent** | **~6.5-7.5GB (swap-thrash risk)** | **~3.5-4.5GB (comfortable)** |

Biggest cuts: headless (+remote GUI) ≈ 1.1-1.3GB; preventing any accidental bot CUDA context ≈ 1GB/process of downside protection; merging the two bots ≈ 0.5GB; ORT-CPU ≈ 0.3GB.
topRecommendations: Run the Jetson headless: `sudo systemctl set-default multi-user.target` (frees ~800MB, zero code). View the dashboard remotely; if gui.py must stay graphical run it on your desktop pointed at the same Alpaca keys, or replace with a small FastAPI status page (~120-140MB) — total ~1.1-1.3GB reclaimed.

Hard-block CUDA in bot processes: export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="" when run_pipeline.py spawns crypto_loop/stock_loop, and make hw_monitor.is_gpu_available() check gpu_lock/no-op when that var is set — one stray call currently costs a permanent ~0.6-1.2GB CUDA context per process (hw_monitor.py:61, imported at trading_utils.py:17).

Replace default zram with NVMe swap: `systemctl disable nvzramconfig`, create 8-16GB swap on NVMe, `vm.swappiness=10-20`. Keeps the Saturday retrain from OOM-killing bots and stops zram stealing CPU (Jetson AI Lab official guidance).

Delete `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = True` (scripts/hypersearch_v2.py:83): your model has no convolutions so it gains nothing, and benchmark mode is a documented cause of transient cuDNN workspace OOM spikes during Optuna trials.

Set `torch.set_num_threads(2)` / OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 in both bots: tiny-LSTM CPU inference is fastest with 1-2 threads and this stops inference stealing cores from the weekly retrain (5-minute change; benchmark 1 vs 2 vs 4).

Merge crypto_loop and stock_loop into one process (two strategy objects on one scheduler, or keep stock as a thread): saves a duplicate torch+pandas+numpy import stack ≈ 0.4-0.7GB and halves Alpaca connection overhead. Your base_loop.py already shares almost all the code.

If you want faster/lighter inference, export the trained models to ONNX (opset>=17) and run onnxruntime CPU in the bots: 2-4x faster than PyTorch eager for small LSTMs and removes the torch import (~150-300MB/process). Skip TensorRT/torch2trt entirely — LSTM conversion pitfalls and batch-1 launch overhead make it net-negative on this model size; torch.jit.trace is the zero-effort fallback.

During the Saturday retrain window only: `nvpmodel` to 25W (best perf/W on JetPack 6.2 Super) or MAXN SUPER + `jetson_clocks` for up to ~1.5-2x training throughput, reverting to 15W after; keep using wait_for_cool_gpu. Requires JetPack >= 6.2 for the Orin Nano Super modes.

Fix the PyTorch 2.8.0 wheel deps system-wide: install cuDSS 0.7.1 and cuSPARSELt (aarch64-jetson builds) into /usr/local/cuda/lib64 + `sudo ldconfig` instead of LD_LIBRARY_PATH exports — run_pipeline-spawned and systemd processes won't inherit shell env, which is how the known libcudss.so.0 ImportError resurfaces in production.

Future-proof training RAM: if harvest sizes grow past ~300k rows, build LSTM input windows per batch (gather indices+offsets inside the train loop, ~8MB/batch) instead of materializing whole folds in SequenceCache (hypersearch_v2.py:320) — and install jetson-stats (`jtop`) to log RAM/temp during retrains so you see headroom, not guesses.

# Evidence Review for the Trader System (researched 2026-06-09)

Note: the live code is ahead of the brief — model_v2.py is a regression LSTM over multi-horizon targets (FORWARD_BARS = 12/18/24/32/48 bars, not next-hour 3-class), model_lgb.py stacks LightGBM, crypto clips are $1,000 (max $3,000) via limit orders, stocks $5,000, and sentiment.py already removed fear-based de-risking. Findings below are against the actual code.

## 1. Transaction costs are the binding constraint (Q2)
Confirmed from Alpaca docs: tier-1 crypto fees (<$100k 30-day volume) are **0.15% maker / 0.25% taker**, falling to 0.00/0.10% only above $100M. A taker round trip costs **50bps = $5.00 per $1,000 clip**; maker, **30bps = $3.00**, plus spread (majors <5bps on tier-1 venues; small alts tens of bps). Break-even win rates with symmetric barriers: ±1% barriers need p>75% (taker) or p>65% (maker); ±2% barriers need p>62.5%/57.5%. Published ML hourly/intraday directional accuracy is 51-55%, so trades only clear costs when the target move is a large multiple of cost: at a realistic 53% hit rate, edge 2p−1=6% of the move means the expected move must be ≥ ~8% of itself... concretely, **target moves ≥ 5% (maker) / 8% (taker) of cost-adjusted scale — i.e., 0.3%/0.06 ≈ 5% is wrong only if barriers symmetric; practical rule: predicted-return floor ≥ 2× round-trip cost (≥60-100bps crypto, ≥20-30bps stocks)**. The default `trade_threshold = 0.15` (15bps) admits negative-expectancy trades on crypto by construction. A walk-forward Bitcoin ML study (arXiv 2606.00060) found sign-based strategies **fail at just 10bps costs** unless a forecast-magnitude execution filter is added — exactly the fix needed here. US equities: liquid high-beta names cost ~2-10bps round trip ($5k clip, spread 1-3bps + ~0.3bps SEC/TAF), so the stock book's hurdle is ~5-10x lower.

## 2. Lopez de Prado techniques — what helps most (Q1)
Priority for THIS system: (a) **Triple-barrier labeling matched to the live exit logic.** The model is trained on raw 12-48-bar forward returns, but positions actually exit via 2×ATR stop / 2:1 TP / trailing stop / 3:50pm flatten — the training objective doesn't match realized PnL. Label with the same barriers the bot trades. (b) **Purged k-fold/walk-forward with embargo ≥ 48 bars**: overlapping multi-horizon targets leak across naive train/val splits, inflating every Optuna trial. (c) **Meta-labeling**: keep LSTM/LGB as the primary side signal; train a secondary classifier on "did this signal make money net of costs" to set size — Hudson & Thames replication showed precision 0.48→0.54 and accuracy 48%→55%; this would replace the ad-hoc confidence multiplier. (d) **Deflated Sharpe Ratio / PBO** (Bailey & Lopez de Prado, SSRN 2460551): hypersearch_v2 runs hundreds of TPE trials; the selected config's backtest Sharpe must be deflated by the number of trials, skew and kurtosis, with CSCV-based PBO < ~25% required before promotion. Sample-uniqueness weights are moderate value; fractional differentiation is low priority (indicator features are already mostly stationary).

## 3. Is there evidence for edge at this horizon? (Q4)
Gross predictability exists but is tiny: best-in-class intraday ML on SPY achieves OOS R² ≈ 0.24% (5-min returns, 2001-2016); the strategy earned 58% annualized **before** costs, 8% after (Sharpe 1.86→0.73). Gao-Han-Li-Zhou (JFE 2018): first half-hour return predicts last half-hour, R² 1.6% (2.6% adding the 12th half-hour) — one of the few robust intraday equity effects. Crypto: Wen-Bouri-Xu-Zhou (2022) find both intraday momentum AND reversal in BTC/ETH/LTC/XRP with sign instability around jumps/FOMC; timing strategies beat buy-and-hold gross. Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen time-series momentum (JFE 2012) is robust but at 1-12 **month** lookbacks. Verdict: the 12-48-hour horizon shift already in the code is the right direction; pure hourly TA prediction is not supported net of retail costs.

## 4. The stock book's structural headwind (Q5)
Lou-Polk-Skouras (JFE 2019): over ~30 years, essentially **all** US equity gains accrued overnight; average intraday returns are flat-to-negative, and momentum profits are earned overnight. Hendershott-Livdan-Rösch (JFE 2020): beta is **positively** priced overnight and **negatively** priced intraday — a long-only, intraday-only book of high-beta names sits in the single worst documented cell of this anomaly. Expected baseline drift is ≤0 before alpha. Flattening at 3:50pm avoids gap risk (real for $25k exposure: single-name gaps of 5-10% happen) but forfeits the part of the day where the premium lives. Evidence-based options: (i) keep day-only but concentrate activity in the open/close half-hours where predictability is documented; (ii) carry a small, capped overnight sleeve (e.g., 20-30% of book, index-hedged or per-name capped at ~$2.5k) to harvest the overnight premium.

## 5. Sentiment gating (Q6)
The current design (FnG fear no longer reduces size; extreme greed ≥90 trims to 0.7x; FnG fed to the model as a feature) is consistent with the evidence. Baker-Wurgler (JoF 2006, replicated through 2023): high sentiment → low subsequent returns for speculative/high-vol assets — contrarian at the top. Crypto FnG literature is mixed: a 2026 study finds returns Granger-cause FnG (not vice versa, no OOS gain daily), while others find 1-day-to-1-week predictive power and that "buy-fear" beats passive. Old behavior (0.3x in extreme fear) was momentum-style de-risking that the contrarian evidence opposes; its removal is correct. A mild contrarian boost in extreme fear is testable but unproven — gate it behind the backtest.

## 6. Model choice (Q7)
Grinsztajn et al. (NeurIPS 2022): tree ensembles are SOTA on tabular data ≲10k rows — exactly this regime (~8,760 hourly crypto bars/yr; ~1,638 stock bars/yr, badly data-starved for an LSTM). M5: **all top-50 entries used LightGBM**; winners were ensembles. M6 (real financial forecasting): only 23.3% of teams beat the forecasting benchmark and **6.7%** beat both forecasting and portfolio benchmarks — strong prior for humility and combination. The existing LSTM+LightGBM stack is well-aligned; if Jetson memory is tight, evidence says drop the LSTM before the LGB.

## 7. Regime and sizing (Q3, Q8, Q9)
Engle's ARCH line is the strongest-evidenced layer in the stack: volatility is forecastable even when returns aren't. Moreira-Muir (JoF 2017): scaling exposure by inverse realized variance raises Sharpe/alpha across market, momentum, carry; 65% lifetime utility gain for a mean-variance investor — with the Cederburg et al. (JFE 2020) caveat that standalone Sharpe gains across 103 strategies are not systematic (positive spanning alphas survive). Vol-targeting in crypto specifically "virtually eliminates crashes" in risk-managed-strategy studies. Keep GARCH sizing; add an explicit portfolio vol target (~15-20% annualized stocks, 30-40% crypto). Regime: Hamilton (1989) MS models are seminal but real-time estimation is unstable; the demonstrably useful live filters are simple — Faber's 200-day MA cut max drawdown 83.7%→42.2% and added ~4%/yr (1972-2006, net). Keep the HMM advisory; gate primarily on realized-vol percentile + daily 200-day trend. Kelly: MacLean-Thorp-Ziemba — full Kelly has a 33% chance of halving before doubling and mean-estimation errors cause severe overbetting; half-Kelly keeps ~75% of growth at far less variance. With noisy ML edges use ≤0.25 Kelly, and size at the **book** level: 10 cryptos correlated 0.7-0.9 to BTC are ~2-3 independent bets (Markowitz), so per-symbol caps alone overstate diversification (the correlation-sizing module is the right instinct — make it the primary cap).

## 8. Backtesting standards (Q10)
There is no cost-aware PnL backtest in the pipeline; models are promoted on fit metrics. Minimum bar before risking capital: event-aware walk-forward simulation with tier-1 fees (15/25bps), spread/partial-fill model for maker orders, and the actual exit stack; vectorbt for fast research sweeps (Numba — fits the Jetson), Nautilus-class realism optional later; report net Sharpe, DSR, PBO, max DD, turnover. Paper-vs-live gap: slippage concentrates in the best trades, so add implementation-shortfall logging (decision price vs fill) now, and require ≥3 months of paper PnL statistically consistent with the backtest before live.

## 9. Nobel anchors, honestly (Q11)
Markowitz: diversification is the only free lunch — but only across uncorrelated bets. Sharpe: judge everything in net Sharpe; market ≈0.4-0.5, an honest retail system net >1 is excellent, backtests >2 are presumptively overfit (deflate them). Fama/Grossman-Stiglitz: at-best ~0.2-2% OOS R² intraday means costs consume most gross edge — design around cost minimization first. Engle: vol forecasting is the most defensible "edge" in this codebase. Kahneman/Thaler/Odean: investors realize gains ~50% more readily than losses (disposition effect costs 3.2-5.7%/yr, Seru et al.); mechanical stops/TPs and the drawdown-deleveraging ladder are the right behavioral encodings — never widen a stop, never re-enter on "revenge" cooldown violations.

## Realistic redesign, prioritized
1. **Cost-aware trade gate**: threshold floor ≥2× venue round-trip (crypto ≥60-100bps predicted, stocks ≥20-30bps); post-only maker orders in crypto; per-symbol daily trade budget. Highest-certainty fix.
2. **Build the net-of-cost walk-forward backtester** (vectorbt + fee/spread model) and make DSR/PBO the promotion criterion in run_pipeline's Saturday retrain — replacing fit-metric selection.
3. **Triple-barrier labels matching live exits + meta-labeler for size**; purged CV with ≥48-bar embargo in hypersearch_v2.
4. **Slow the crypto book**: decisions on closed hourly bars, 12-48h holds (already the model horizon), fewer/larger conviction trades.
5. **Restructure the stock book** around documented effects (open/close half-hour momentum; optional capped overnight sleeve) instead of all-day high-beta longs into a negative intraday beta premium.
6. **Unify sizing into ≤0.25-Kelly with a portfolio vol target**, correlation-aware book caps; keep GARCH, demote HMM to advisory, add 200-day trend filter.
7. **Measure**: implementation shortfall per trade, monthly DSR recompute, paper-vs-backtest tracking error — go-live only when consistent.
topRecommendations: Raise the trade gate to a cost-aware floor: require predicted net move >= 2x round-trip cost (crypto: >=60-100bps given Alpaca tier-1 0.15%/0.25% maker/taker; stocks: >=20-30bps). The current trade_threshold default of 0.15 (15bps) admits structurally negative-expectancy crypto trades.

Build a net-of-cost walk-forward backtester (vectorbt + 15/25bps fees, spread, maker partial-fill model, the real ATR-stop/TP/flatten exit stack) and gate every Saturday retrain promotion on Deflated Sharpe Ratio and Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBO < ~25%), not fit metrics - Optuna's hundreds of trials guarantee selection bias otherwise (Bailey & Lopez de Prado).

Adopt triple-barrier labels that mirror the live exit logic (2x ATR stop, 2:1 TP, time/flatten barrier) so the model is trained on the PnL it will actually realize, instead of raw 12-48-bar forward returns.

Add purged cross-validation with an embargo >= 48 bars (the longest forward horizon) in scripts/hypersearch_v2.py - overlapping multi-horizon targets currently leak label information into validation folds, inflating every trial.

Add a meta-labeling stage: keep LSTM/LightGBM as the primary direction signal and train a secondary classifier on 'did this signal profit net of costs' to set position size (replicated gains: precision 0.48->0.54), replacing the ad-hoc confidence multiplier.

Slow the crypto book: act only on closed hourly bars with 12-48h intended holds (matching FORWARD_BARS), post-only maker orders, and a per-symbol daily trade budget - walk-forward BTC ML studies show sign strategies die at even 10bps costs without a magnitude filter.

Restructure the stock book around documented intraday effects: long-only intraday high-beta fights a negative intraday beta premium (Hendershott et al. 2020) and a market whose gains accrue almost entirely overnight (Lou-Polk-Skouras 2019). Concentrate activity in the open/close half-hours (Gao et al. 2018, R^2 1.6-2.6%) and consider a small capped overnight sleeve to harvest the overnight premium.

Unify the sizing stack into fractional Kelly <= 0.25 with an explicit portfolio volatility target (~15-20% annualized stocks, 30-40% crypto) and correlation-aware book-level caps - 10 BTC-correlated cryptos are only ~2-3 independent Markowitz bets (MacLean-Thorp-Ziemba: full Kelly halves your bankroll before doubling 33% of the time).

Keep the GARCH vol-targeting layer (Engle; Moreira-Muir 2017 - the best-evidenced component) but demote the HMM to advisory and gate regime primarily on realized-vol percentile plus a 200-day MA trend filter (Faber: max drawdown 83.7%->42.2%).

Keep the current sentiment design (no fear de-risking, trim at extreme greed) - it matches Baker-Wurgler contrarian evidence; FnG mostly reacts to price in crypto. Log implementation shortfall (decision price vs fill) per trade now and require >=3 months of paper results statistically consistent with the backtest before any live capital.

# LLM-in-Trading Research Report — for the Jetson trader system
(Current code facts used: analyst gate fires every 600s per loop = ~183 calls/day (144 crypto + ~39 stock); sentiment chunks ≤80 articles/call; backfill worker at 8 RPM; $1.00/day cost cap; Gemini-only urllib client in `llm_client.py`; `json_mode` sets only `responseMimeType` and is skipped for "pro" models; system prompt sent as fake user/model turns; hardcoded `_PRICING` table.)

## 1. Literature: what's established
**Lopez-Lira & Tang (arXiv 2304.07619, SSRN 4412788).** GPT headline scores predicted next-day drift (esp. small caps and negative news). Established caveats from the published version itself: Sharpe decayed 6.54 (2021Q4) → 3.68 (2022) → 2.33 (2023) → 1.22 (Jan–May 2024) — strong post-publication/post-ChatGPT decay; ~190%/day turnover; cumulative return falls from 350% at 10 bps costs to ~50% at 25 bps. For your large-cap top-47 universe with 10-min cadence, the exploitable edge is mostly in the *negative-news* tail, which supports your veto design more than the boost side. **Glasserman & Lin (arXiv 2309.17322)** show look-ahead bias and a "distraction effect" inflate LLM backtests when ticker names are visible — never trust an LLM backtest over the model's training window. **Replications** (Modern Finance "Could ChatGPT have earned abnormal returns?", Chen et al. arXiv 2502.10008) find weaker/regime-dependent results.
**FinBERT vs general LLMs.** Mixed but consistent pattern: zero-shot GPT underperforms fine-tuned FinBERT on explicit-label benchmarks (e.g., 54.2% vs 63.3% accuracy in MDPI 2025 sector study), while few-shot GPT-4o matches fine-tuned FinBERT (arXiv 2410.01987) and is better on implied/contextual sentiment; FinBERT over-labels implicit sentiment "neutral". FinGPT-style LoRA-tuned small models match GPT-4 on FPB-class benchmarks. Implication: a cheap general LLM **with few-shot anchors** is a sound replacement for your keyword scorer; FinBERT isn't worth deploying on the Jetson alongside your stack.
**Agentic frameworks.** TradingAgents (2412.20138), FinMem (2311.13743), FinAgent report strong backtests, but **FINSABER (2505.07078)** — 20 years, 100+ symbols — shows the advantage largely disappears out-of-sample: FinMem only consistently won on TSLA; LLM strategies were too conservative in bulls and too aggressive in bears with large drawdowns. **TradeTrap (2512.02261)** shows LLM trading agents are unreliable under realistic perturbations. Components that survive scrutiny: structured memory of past trades (you already have `trade_memory.py`), separating direction from sizing, and risk-rule gates. The "many debating agents" layer is mostly hype at your scale and budget.

## 2. Best-practice role + how to prove it helps
Evidence favors LLM as a **bounded risk-gate/multiplier overlay**, not a signal generator: keep the LSTM as the only entry signal; LLM may only scale 0–1.5x and veto. Two tightenings supported by the literature's asymmetry (negative news predicts better): (a) give the veto/downscale side full authority but cap the boost side (e.g., ≤1.25x) so a hallucinated bull case can't double risk; (b) treat the LLM "s" as ordinal, not cardinal — bucket it (veto / reduce / neutral / boost) rather than multiplying by a pseudo-precise float. Post-trade analyst (journaling "why it worked/failed" into `trade_memory`) is the lowest-risk, clearly-positive role.
**Evaluation (the part most shops skip):** you cannot know the gate helps without counterfactuals. Concretely: (1) every cycle, log per symbol {ml_signal, llm_s, multiplier_applied, action_taken, action_if_no_llm} to the JSONL journal; (2) for blocked/downsized trades, replay your own ATR stop / 1.5x trail / 2:1 TP rules on subsequent bars to compute counterfactual P&L of the foregone size; (3) A/B: hash(symbol, ISO-week) % 2 → multiplier active vs forced 1.0 (keep only the catastrophic veto ≤0.15 in both arms), compare expectancy/Sharpe with paired bootstrap after ≥200 trades/arm; (4) report "LLM uplift" = realized − counterfactual, net of the ~5–10 bps spread your fills cross. This is established practice (shadow/champion-challenger), not speculation.

## 3. Structured JSON per provider (verified mid-2026)
- **Gemini:** structured outputs via `responseMimeType: application/json` + schema (`responseJsonSchema` / `responseFormat` schema in REST) are supported on the whole current lineup — 2.5 Pro/Flash/Flash-Lite, 3.1 Pro Preview, 3.1 Flash-Lite, 3.5 Flash — **including thinking/Pro models**. Your `if json_mode and "pro" not in model` guard is obsolete; passing a full schema (object keyed by symbol; `s` number, `bull`/`bear`/`r` strings) eliminates the brace-repair/truncation parser in `llm_analyst.py` and the array-format workaround you patched. Current pricing ($/1M in/out): 2.5 Flash-Lite **$0.10/$0.40**, 2.5 Flash **$0.30/$2.50**, 3.1 Flash-Lite **$0.25/$1.50**, 3.5 Flash **$1.50/$9.00**, 2.5 Pro $1.25/$10. Your `_PRICING` table (0.075/0.30, 0.15/0.60) understates real spend ~2–4x — your $1/day cap triggers later than you think.
- **OpenAI:** Responses API `text.format` (or Chat Completions `response_format`) with `json_schema` + `strict: true` gives schema-guaranteed output. Current cheap tier: **gpt-5.4-nano $0.20/$1.25** (cached input $0.02; released 2026-03-19; supports structured outputs + tools), gpt-5.4-mini $0.75/$4.50, flagship gpt-5.4 $2.50/$15.
- **Anthropic:** structured outputs are GA via `output_config: {format: {type: "json_schema", schema: ...}}` on `messages.create` (old `output_format` deprecated); supported on Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.8. Cheap tier: **claude-haiku-4-5 $1.00/$5.00**. Tool-use with `strict: true` input schemas is the alternative JSON path. At your volume Haiku is ~$2.75/day for the analyst role — fallback only.

## 4. Prompt caching — mostly NOT applicable here
- Anthropic: `cache_control: {type: ephemeral}` — reads 0.1x, writes 1.25x (5-min TTL) — **but minimum cacheable prefix on Haiku 4.5 is 4,096 tokens**; your ~500-token system prompt will silently never cache.
- OpenAI: automatic prefix caching, cached input billed at 10% on the 5.4/5.5 family (was 50% on older models), ≥1,024-token prefixes.
- Gemini: implicit caching is on by default for 2.5+ on paid tier (~75–90% off cached tokens); minimums 2,048 (2.5 Flash/Pro) and 4,096 (3.5 Flash/3.1 Pro); explicit caches default 1h TTL + storage fees.
Established conclusion for THIS system: your stable prefix (system prompt) is far below every minimum, and 10-min call spacing exceeds Anthropic's 5-min TTL. Don't engineer for caching; just (a) move the system prompt into Gemini's `systemInstruction` field (replacing the fake "Understood." turns — also improves quality) and (b) keep stable content first so implicit caching kicks in for free if prompts ever grow past 2K tokens.

## 5. Batch APIs for the sentiment backfill
All three are ~50% off: **Gemini Batch** (flash-lite $0.05/$0.20, target ≤24h, usually much faster; separate enqueued-token quota — doesn't consume your live RPM/RPD), **Anthropic Message Batches** (50%; ≤100k requests/256MB; most <1h; results kept 29 days; Haiku effective $0.50/$2.50), **OpenAI Batch** (50%, 24h window). The backfill worker's 8-RPM loop competes with live trading calls and burns interactive RPD. Moving backfill to nightly Gemini Batch jobs costs ~$0.03–0.12/day at 1–2k articles/day and frees the entire interactive quota for the loops. This is the single clearest win in the whole review.

## 6. Local LLM on the Orin Nano 8GB — not worth it as primary
Measured numbers (Orin Nano 8GB): ~5.2GB usable after OS; 68 GB/s memory bandwidth makes inference memory-bound (~21% HW efficiency). Ollama Q4: Qwen3-0.6B 38.8 t/s, Qwen2.5-0.5B 35.2 t/s, Gemma3-1B 26.3 t/s, Gemma3n-E2B 9.0 t/s; vLLM 2–6x slower. **Gemma3-4B Q4_K_M (2.4GB) OOMs at every power mode** once KV cache + CUDA overhead are added; Qwen3-4B Q3 needs layer-offload tricks. Jetson AI Lab cites Llama 3.2 3B at 27.7 t/s — but on an otherwise idle Super at MAXN. With your trading stack holding 3–4GB (PyTorch, dual LSTMs, GUI, weekly Optuna retrains via `gpu_lock.py`), only ~1B-class models fit safely, and 1B models are markedly worse at financial-news nuance than 2.5 Flash-Lite — while the free tier already gives 15 RPM/1,000 RPD at $0. Verdict (established): keep cloud primary. Optional: `ollama run qwen3:0.6b` as an *offline* upgrade over the keyword fallback when the 429 circuit-breaker trips — speculative value, test before adopting.

## 7. Free-tier limits (mid-2026)
Official docs no longer print numbers (live in AI Studio dashboard). Best third-party compilations (Jan–May 2026): free tier — 2.5 Flash-Lite **15 RPM / 250K TPM / ~1,000 RPD**, 2.5 Flash 10 RPM / ~250 RPD, **Pro removed from free tier** (May 2026); Gemini 3 Flash free ~10 RPM/1,500 RPD per one source (unverified). Tier-1 paid: ~300 RPM on the flash family. Implications: your `_FREE_TIER_BUDGETS` (pro 50, flash 500, flash-lite 1,500) and 10-RPM free limiter are stale — on free tier, pro will 429 and flash-lite RPD is ~1,000. Your 183 analyst calls/day fit free tier only if the backfill worker is capped (~600 calls/day) or moved to batch. The 30s loop cadence is irrelevant since the analyst gate is 600s — good design.

## 8. Sentiment-scoring prompt practice
Established failure modes: position/order bias in long batched lists, label bias, framing sycophancy (negative-toned prompts measurably reduce factual accuracy ~8%), non-determinism, and scale drift (clustering at 0.5/round numbers — your system prompt already fights this well). Mitigations with evidence: (1) fixed scale with **3–5 few-shot anchor examples** pinning what −0.8/−0.3/0/+0.3/+0.8 mean; (2) require per-item `evidence` span + categorical label alongside the number (improves calibration and auditability); (3) batch by **stable IDs** (`{"id": 17, "score": ...}`) not order, and keep batches ≤20–30 headlines — your 80-article chunks invite position bias and MAX_TOKENS truncation (which you currently discard wholesale); (4) temperature 0–0.2 (Gemini still non-deterministic; don't assume reproducibility); (5) neutral framing ("score the sentiment" not "find the risks"); (6) periodic shuffle-consistency check: rescore a shuffled batch weekly and alert if mean |Δ| > 0.1.

## Cost model at current volume (computed)
Analyst (~183 calls/day, ~0.92M in/0.37M out tokens/day): 2.5 Flash-Lite **~$7/mo**; 3.1 Flash-Lite ~$23/mo; gpt-5.4-nano ~$19/mo; 2.5 Flash ~$36/mo (breaches your $1/day cap); Haiku 4.5 ~$82/mo. Live sentiment ~$2–4/mo on flash-lite; batch backfill ~$1–4/mo. **Recommended defaults: analyst = gemini-2.5-flash-lite with `responseJsonSchema` (upgrade to gemini-3.1-flash-lite if A/B shows quality gain justifies ~$16/mo extra); sentiment = gemini-2.5-flash-lite; backfill = Gemini Batch on 2.5-flash-lite. Fallback chain: gpt-5.4-nano → claude-haiku-4-5, both with strict JSON schema. Total ≈ $10–15/month paid tier-1, or $0 on free tier with backfill throttled to stay under 1,000 RPD.**
topRecommendations: Keep the LLM as a bounded overlay, never a signal source: literature (FINSABER 2505.07078, TradeTrap 2512.02261, Lopez-Lira's own Sharpe decay 6.54→1.22) supports veto+multiplier only. Make it asymmetric — full authority to veto/downsize (negative news has the strongest evidence), cap the boost side at ~1.25x instead of 1.5x, and bucket 's' into {veto, reduce, neutral, boost} rather than trusting float precision.

Prove the gate earns its keep: log per-cycle {ml_signal, llm_s, multiplier, action_taken, action_without_llm} to the trade journal, replay your own ATR-stop/trailing/TP rules to compute counterfactual P&L of blocked/downsized trades, and A/B by hash(symbol, week) with multiplier on vs forced 1.0 (≥200 trades/arm, paired bootstrap on expectancy).

Replace json_mode with real schema enforcement: send responseJsonSchema (object keyed by symbol: s number, bull/bear/r strings) on ALL Gemini models — the 'pro doesn't support it' guard in _call_gemini is wrong per current docs — and delete the brace-repair/truncation parser paths in llm_analyst.py and sentiment.py once enforced.

Move the backfill worker from the 8-RPM live loop to Gemini Batch API jobs (flash-lite $0.05/$0.20 per 1M, 50% off, ≤24h turnaround, separate quota): ~$0.03-0.12/day, zero contention with live trading RPM/RPD. Use Anthropic Message Batches (Haiku 4.5 at effective $0.50/$2.50, most batches <1h) only as cross-provider fallback.

Default models per role: analyst=gemini-2.5-flash-lite (~$7/mo at your 183 calls/day), sentiment=gemini-2.5-flash-lite, backfill=Gemini Batch flash-lite; fallback chain gpt-5.4-nano ($0.20/$1.25, strict json_schema via Responses API) then claude-haiku-4-5 ($1/$5, output_config json_schema). Expected total $10-15/month on paid tier-1; A/B gemini-3.1-flash-lite ($0.25/$1.50, ~$23/mo) for the analyst role before paying for it.

Fix the stale cost table and estimation in llm_client.py: 2.5 Flash is now $0.30/$2.50 and Flash-Lite $0.10/$0.40 (your 0.15/0.60 and 0.075/0.30 understate spend 2-4x against the $1/day cap), and read usageMetadata token counts from the Gemini response instead of chars/4.

Use Gemini's systemInstruction field instead of the fake user/'Understood.' turns in _call_gemini — better instruction adherence and a stable prefix for free implicit caching (75-90% off cached tokens, automatic on paid 2.5+). Do NOT engineer prompt caching beyond this: your ~500-token prefix is below every provider minimum (Gemini 2,048; Anthropic Haiku 4,096; OpenAI 1,024) and the 600s call spacing exceeds Anthropic's 5-min TTL.

Skip local LLM as primary on the 8GB Orin Nano: ~5.2GB usable, 68GB/s memory-bound, Gemma3-4B Q4 OOMs alongside a 3-4GB trading stack, and viable 0.6-1B models (Qwen3-0.6B 38.8 t/s, Gemma3-1B 26.3 t/s via Ollama) underperform flash-lite on financial nuance. Harden sentiment scoring: cut chunks from 80 articles to ≤25, key batch items by stable id (not order), add 3-5 few-shot anchor examples pinning the -1..+1 scale, require a short evidence span + categorical label per item, set temperature 0-0.2, and run a weekly shuffle-consistency check (alert if mean |Δscore| > 0.1).

# Alpaca Infrastructure Research — trader system (2026-06-09)

## 1. alpaca-trade-api is dead; this repo has a live dependency conflict
- `alpaca-trade-api` last release: **v3.2.0, Jan 12, 2024**. Repo not archived but deprecation notice says maintenance ended **end of 2022**; zero releases in ~2.5 years. PyPI page carries the deprecation banner pointing to alpaca-py.
- **Concrete breakage in THIS repo**: alpaca-trade-api pins `websockets>=9.0,<11`, `aiohttp>=3.8.3,<4`, `urllib3>1.24,<2`, `PyYAML==6.0.1`, `msgpack==1.0.3`. Your `requirements.txt` simultaneously requires `websockets>=12.0` — **unsatisfiable**; pip either errors or silently installs websockets 10.x. The `urllib3<2` pin also fights the modern ecosystem (your Mac has urllib3 2.6.3). Forum reports confirm install failures on Python 3.12+ (Jetson's 3.10 is OK for now).
- REST v2 trading/data endpoints still work in 2026 (your `>=3.0.0` floor means crypto data uses the current v1beta3 path), so nothing is broken *today* — the risk is dependency rot and no fixes if Alpaca changes anything.
- **Migration path**: `alpaca-py` **v0.43.4 (Apr 29, 2026)**, Python 3.8–3.14, pydantic models. Mapping: `REST.submit_order(**kwargs)` → `TradingClient.submit_order(MarketOrderRequest/LimitOrderRequest(..., order_class=OrderClass.BRACKET, take_profit=TakeProfitRequest, stop_loss=StopLossRequest))`; `get_bars` → `StockHistoricalDataClient.get_stock_bars(StockBarsRequest)`; `get_crypto_bars` → `CryptoHistoricalDataClient`; trade updates → `TradingStream`. Only 5 files import the old SDK directly (`gui.py`, `trading_utils.py`, `scripts/connection_test.py`, both harvest scripts) plus `self.api.*` calls in the loops — a contained refactor.

## 2. Crypto economics (current, docs.alpaca.markets/us/docs/crypto-fees)
- **Fee tiers (30-day volume, maker/taker)**: $0–100K: **15/25 bps**; 100K–500K: 12/22; 500K–1M: 10/20; 1M–10M: 8/18; 10M–25M: 5/15; 25M–50M: 2/13; 50M–100M: 2/12; $100M+: 0/10. Fees charged **in the asset received** (buy ETH/USD → fee in ETH), posted end-of-day; query Activities API `activity_type=CFEE`.
- **Impact on crypto_loop**: $250 taker market orders cost 25 bps/side = **$0.625/side, $1.25 (0.50%) per round trip**, before spread. Your model needs >~0.6% edge per round trip. Resting GTC limit orders earn maker (15 bps) instead.
- **Venue/spreads**: Orders execute on Alpaca's own venue ("ALPACA" exchange); v1beta3 market data is from that venue. Forum history reports spreads materially wider than Coinbase/Kraken (extreme reports up to 2.5% on BTC/USD in stressed periods; threads #7094, #14538). Coinbase Advanced is 40/60 bps fees at the lowest tier with ~1bp BTC spreads; Kraken Pro 25/40 bps. Established: Alpaca's headline fees beat both at tier 1; speculation (verify by sampling `latest_quote` spreads): all-in cost on alts is likely worse on Alpaca due to spread.
- **Universe/sizes**: 20+ assets, ~56 pairs (USD/USDT/USDC/BTC quotes); min order = dynamic **$1 notional equivalent** (`min_order_size`, e.g. BTC 0.0001); max **$200k notional/order**; no margin, no shorting.
- **Order types for crypto: market, limit, stop_limit ONLY. No bracket, OCO, OTO, stop, or trailing-stop. `time_in_force`: `gtc` and `ioc` ONLY** (no day/fok). Your software-side stop/trail/TP for crypto is the only possible design — correct as built.

## 3. Equity microstructure, fees, PDT
- **Sell-side fees (Alpaca fee schedule, revised June 1, 2026)**: SEC fee **$20.60 per $1M** (back from $0.00; effective Apr 4, 2026, per FINRA notice) ≈ $0.05 per $2,500 sale; FINRA TAF **$0.000195/share, max $9.79, rounded up to next penny** ≈ $0.01 for a 10–50 share lot; CAT fee $0.000003/share both sides (daily-aggregated). Full 10-position daily flatten ≈ **$0.60–0.80/day** — small but nonzero; paper simulates none of it.
- **PDT is RETIRED — 5 days ago.** FINRA's intraday margin framework took effect **June 4, 2026**: no $25k minimum; margin accounts with ≥**$2,000** equity get 4x **intraday buying power**; pre-trade checks reject orders creating an Intraday Margin Deficit; repeated unmet IMD calls within 5 business days → 90-day restriction. **A live margin account under $25k flattening 10 positions daily is no longer blocked** (subject to intraday BP). A *cash* account is still bound by T+1 settled funds — ~$25k cash needed to redeploy $25k daily without good-faith violations, so use margin. **API fields `pattern_day_trader`, `daytrade_count`, `daytrading_buying_power` etc. are deprecated and removed July 6, 2026** — grep your code/GUI for them now.
- **Paper fill simulation (official docs)**: orders fill when marketable against **NBBO of your feed (IEX on free plan)**; deliberate random **partial fills ~10%** of the time; **no** market impact, queue position, slippage/latency, liquidity cap (fills can exceed displayed size), regulatory fees, dividends, or borrow fees. Gotchas where paper flatters live: limit orders "fill" at first touch (live needs queue priority); market orders fill at stale/wide IEX quotes on thin names; crypto fees likely absent (verify: check paper account for CFEE activities).

## 4. Market data: IEX vs SIP, rate limits, streaming
- **IEX free feed ≈ 2–3% of consolidated volume** (Alpaca's own FAQ example: 12,630 IEX trades vs 535,136 SIP for FB). Quotes can be stale/off-NBBO; minute bars missing for thin symbols — material when scoring 47 symbols hourly.
- **Free workaround (established, market-data FAQ)**: historical queries may use **`feed=sip` when `end` is ≥15 minutes old** — full-market hourly bars, free. `/v2/stocks/bars` defaults: `feed=sip`, `adjustment=raw`, `limit` up to **10,000/page**. One multi-symbol request covers all 47 tickers.
- **Plans**: Basic free = IEX real-time, **200 data req/min, 30 websocket symbols, 1 connection** (error 406 on a 2nd, 405 over symbol limit, 407 slow client, 409 insufficient subscription); **Algo Trader Plus $99/mo** = real-time SIP, unlimited calls/symbols, OPRA options. **Trading API is 200 req/min regardless of plan** (429 over). Both loops + GUI + sentiment backfill share one account's budgets.
- **Architecture**: at 10–47 symbols/30s, REST polling (~20–40 req/min) is fine and simpler. Websockets don't replay missed messages on reconnect (REST backfill required), and Basic allows only one data connection — so two loops can't each hold a stream. Highest-value stream: **`trade_updates` (TradingStream)** to replace `manage_order_lifecycle` 2s polling and catch server-side bracket fills.

## 5. Bracket semantics and the 3:50pm flatten — two live bugs in this repo
- Bracket = OTO+OCO: legs activate after entry fills; partial TP fill auto-shrinks the stop leg; **canceling any leg cancels the whole group**; legs replaceable via PATCH (not for notional orders); TIF day/gtc; no extended hours; **GTC legs auto-cancel after 90 days**. Trailing stops: equities only (day/gtc, never trigger outside RTH, not yet allowed as a bracket leg); **not supported for crypto**.
- Manual close while children live → **403 "insufficient qty available"** (shares held for orders) or **403 "potential wash trade detected"** (opposite-side open orders; native bracket/OCO/trailing groups are exempt). Alpaca documents the **cancel→close race**: cancellation is async (`pending_cancel`); an immediate sell can still reject.
- **Bug 1 — `stock_loop.py:141-180` `flatten_before_close()` sells without canceling `info.stop_order_id`** (bracket children or upgraded trailing stop) → expect 403 insufficient-qty/wash-trade rejections at 3:50pm. **Bug 2 — `stock_loop.py:279-290`** cancels the stop then sells immediately with no cancel-confirmation poll (the race above). Fix: cancel, poll until `canceled`, then sell — or use `DELETE /v2/positions?cancel_orders=true` (`close_all_positions(cancel_orders=True)`, returns 207 multi-status) for the EOD flatten.
- **Bug 3 — half-days**: `FLATTEN_HOUR=15:50` and `check_market_hours` (stock_loop.py:80-91) are wall-clock only. On 1:00pm early closes (e.g., Nov 27 and Dec 24, 2026) the 15:50–16:00 window is after close → **positions held overnight with GTC bracket legs live**, exactly the gap risk the design forbids. It also "trades" on weekday holidays (day limit orders queue for the next session). Use `GET /v2/clock` (`is_open`, `next_close` — reflects early closes) and `GET /v2/calendar` (per-day `open`/`close`, early closes show 13:00; `session_open/close` for extended) and flatten at `next_close − 10min`.

## 6. Account/safety APIs
`GET /v2/account`: `status`, `trading_blocked`, `account_blocked`, `trade_suspended_by_user`, `equity`, `last_equity` (right baseline for your 5% breaker), `buying_power` (the only forward-compatible BP field after July 6, 2026). Corporate actions (`/v2/corporate_actions/announcements`) are irrelevant while flat daily — but the half-day bug above can leave overnight positions exposed to splits/dividends, which would corrupt `_reconstruct_positions`. Crypto positions persist by design; no corporate actions there.

## 7. yfinance vs Alpaca for training data
- yfinance (now **1.4.1, May 28, 2026**): `1h` interval hard-capped at **730 days** (Yahoo limit); aggressive **429/YFRateLimitError** blocks since 2025 (it scrapes Yahoo; IP bans observed); `auto_adjust=True` became the default (intraday bars remain split/dividend-inconsistent vs daily); missing hourly bars on thin tickers.
- Alpaca historical is the better primary (your `data_sources.py` already prefers it): stocks free via **SIP** (end ≥15 min old), 7+ years, 1Min/1Hour/1Day, 10k bars/page. **Critical: default `adjustment=raw`** — request `adjustment='all'` or splits (e.g., a 10:1) will inject fake −90% moves into training. Crypto bars (v1beta3) are free and from the very venue you trade — better than yfinance's Yahoo composite for this purpose. Keep yfinance as fallback only.
topRecommendations: Fix the EOD flatten order-handling bug now: flatten_before_close() (stock_loop.py:141-180) never cancels bracket/trailing children before selling -> 403 insufficient-qty/wash-trade rejections; cancel each child, poll until status=='canceled', then sell, or use close_all_positions(cancel_orders=True) (DELETE /v2/positions?cancel_orders=true).

Fix half-day/holiday handling: replace hardcoded 15:50/16:00 wall-clock logic with GET /v2/clock next_close (reflects 1pm early closes, e.g. Nov 27 and Dec 24, 2026) and GET /v2/calendar; flatten at next_close-10min and skip holidays entirely.

Migrate the 5 importing files to alpaca-py 0.43.4: alpaca-trade-api 3.2.0 (Jan 2024) is unmaintained and its websockets<11/urllib3<2 pins are unsatisfiable against your own requirements.txt websockets>=12.0 (pip silently downgrades today).

Remove any reliance on pattern_day_trader/daytrade_count account fields before Alpaca deletes them on July 6, 2026; PDT itself was retired June 4, 2026 - a live MARGIN account >= $2,000 equity can now run your 10-roundtrips/day stock strategy (use margin, not cash, to avoid T+1 settled-funds limits).

Model crypto costs explicitly: 25 bps taker per side = $1.25 (0.50%) per $250 round trip plus Alpaca-venue spread; raise the crypto trade threshold to require >~0.6% expected move, prefer resting GTC limit entries to earn 15 bps maker pricing, and reconcile CFEE activities into the trade journal (paper does not deduct them).

Switch hourly stock scoring to SIP historical bars (free when end >= 15-16 min old; feed defaults to sip on /v2/stocks/bars) and batch all 47 symbols in one multi-symbol request instead of 47 calls - IEX covers only ~2-3% of consolidated volume and drops bars on thin names.

Always request adjustment='all' on Alpaca stock bars for training data (default is raw; unadjusted splits inject fake +/-90% moves into LSTM training labels); keep yfinance only as fallback with explicit auto_adjust and backoff for 429/YFRateLimitError, and remember its 730-day 1h cap.

Replace manage_order_lifecycle 2-second REST polling with a single shared TradingStream (trade_updates websocket) process - one connection per account, JSON protocol, catches server-side bracket/trailing fills the loops currently miss between cycles; REST-backfill order state after any reconnect since missed events are not replayed.

Add a shared token-bucket rate limiter across stock_loop, crypto_loop, GUI, and the sentiment backfill worker: trading API is 200 req/min per account on every plan and Basic market data is also 200/min (429 + backoff handling); upgrade to Algo Trader Plus ($99/mo, real-time SIP, unlimited data calls) only if you go live on equities.

Before trusting paper P&L, haircut results for known paper-vs-live flattery: fills at stale IEX NBBO with no queue position, no slippage/market impact, fills beyond displayed liquidity, random 10% partial fills, and zero fees - apply ~5-10 bps/side haircut on equities and 25 bps + measured spread on crypto when evaluating strategy viability.
